[P734|Heading 1] Basic Configuration Guide
[P735|Heading 2] Configuring System Management
[P736|Heading 3] Overview
[P737|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P738|Normal] Banner function is used for configuring messages on the devices. User can specify any messages to notify other users. Improper operations might cause critical situation such as service interrupt, in this case, a notification in advance is necessary. (E.g. to notify users “Don’t reboot”)
[P739|Body Text] Three types of messages are supported by now:
[P740|Item List] MOTD(message-of-the-day). Messages will display on the terminal when user connect to the device.
[P741|Item List] login banner. Messages will display on the terminal when user login to the device. “Login mode” is required for displaying this message. Please reference the section of “Configuring User Management”.
[P742|Item List] exec banner. Messages will display on the terminal when user enter the EXEC mode.
[P743|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P744|Normal] This function displays notification on the terminal to reduce misoperation.
[P745|Heading 3] Configuration
[P746|Heading 4] Configuring a MOTD Login Banner
[P747|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P748|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P749|Heading 5] step 2 Create the notification
[P750|Normal] User can create a notification (one line or multiple lines) to display on all connected terminals. In the following example, the delimiting character is #. All characters between two delimiting characters will display on the terminals when user connect the device.
[P751|Body Text] The message length is at most 99 lines with 1023 character in each line.
[P752|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# banner motd # This is a switch #
[P753|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P754|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# exit
[P755|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P756|Normal] Use the following command to display the configuration:
[P757|Terminal Display] switch# show running
banner motd ^C
 This is a switch
^C
[P758|Heading 4] Configuring a Login Banner
[P759|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P760|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P761|Heading 5] step 2 Create the notification
[P762|Normal] User can create a notification (one line or multiple lines) to display on all connected terminals. “Login mode” is required for displaying this message. Please reference the section of “Configuring User Management”.
[P763|Body Text] In the following example, the delimiting character is #. All characters between two delimiting characters will display on the terminals when user connect the device.
[P764|Body Text] The message length is at most 99 lines with 1023 character in each line.
[P765|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# banner login # admin login #
[P766|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P767|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# exit
[P768|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P769|Normal] Use the following command to display the configuration
[P770|Terminal Display] switch# show running
banner login ^C
 admin login 
^C
[P771|Heading 4] Configuring an Exec Banner
[P772|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P773|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P774|Heading 5] step 2 Create the notification
[P775|Normal] User can create a notification (one line or multiple lines) to display on all connected terminals. In the following example, the delimiting character is #. All characters between two delimiting characters will display on the terminals when user enter the EXEC mode.
[P776|Body Text] The message length is at most 99 lines with 1023 character in each line.
[P777|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# banner exec # do not reboot! #
[P778|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P779|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# exit
[P780|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P781|Normal] Use the following command to display the configuration:
[P782|Terminal Display] switch# show running
banner exec ^C
 do not reboot! 
^C
[P783|Heading 3] Application cases
[P784|Heading 4] Case 1: mark the usage of the device
[P785|Normal] Set the MOTD message as “This is a switch of some area/department”, user can see this message when connect to the device. If the user needs to operate a switch of another department, he can realize that he connected to a wrong device and stop misoperation.
[P786|Heading 5] Configuration steps
[P787|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# banner motd # This is a switch of IT DEPARTMENT ！！！ #
Switch(config)# exit
[P788|Heading 5] Configuration files
[P789|Terminal Display] switch# show running
banner motd ^C
 This is a switch of IT DEPARTMENT ！！！
^C
[P790|Heading 2] Configuring User Management
[P791|Heading 3] Overview
[P792|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P793|Normal] User management increases the security of the system by keeping the unauthorized users from guessing the password. The user is limited to a specific number of attempts to successfully log in to the switch.
[P794|Body Text] There are three load modes in the switch.
[P795|Item List] In “no login” mode, anyone can load the switch without authentication.
[P796|Item List] In “login” mode, there is only one default user.
[P797|Item List] In “login local” mode, if you want to load the switch you need to have a user account. Local user authentication uses local user accounts and passwords that you create to validate the login attempts of local users. Each switch has a maximum of 32 local user accounts. Before you can enable local user authentication, you must define at least one local user account. You can set up local user accounts by creating a unique username and password combination for each local user. Each username must be fewer than 32 characters. You can configure each local user account with a privilege level; the valid privilege levels are 1 or 4. Once a local user is logged in, only the commands those are available for that privilege level can be displayed.
[P798|Normal] There is only one user can enter the configure mode at the same time.
[P799|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P800|Normal] N/A
[P801|Heading 3] Configuration
[P802|Heading 4] Configuring the user management in login local mode
[P803|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P804|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P805|Heading 5] step 2 et username and password
[P806|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# username testname privilege 4 password 123abc<>
[P807|Heading 5] step 3 Enter the configure mode and set user management mode
[P808|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# line vty 0 7
Switch(config-line)# login local
Switch(config-line)# exit
[P809|Heading 5] step 4 Exit the configure mode
[P810|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# exit
[P811|Heading 5] step 5 Validation
[P812|Normal] After the above setting, login the switch will need a username and password, and user can login with the username and password created before. This is a sample output of the login prompt.
[P813|Terminal Display] Username: 
[P814|Normal] After the input the username, a password is required.
[P815|Terminal Display] Username: testname
Password:
[P816|Normal] Authentication succeed:
[P817|Terminal Display] Password: 

Switch# 
[P818|Heading 4] Configuring the user management in login mode
[P819|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P820|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P821|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the configure mode and set password
[P822|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# line vty 0 7
Switch(config-line)# line-password abc
Switch(config-line)# login
[P823|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P824|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# exit
[P825|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P826|Normal] After the above setting, login the switch will need the line password, and user can login with the password created before. This is a sample output of the login prompt.
[P827|Terminal Display] Password:
[P828|Heading 4] Configuring Password recovery procedure
[P829|Normal] If the password is forgotten unfortunately, it can be recovered by following steps.
[P830|Heading 5] Step 1 Power on the system. Boot loader will start to run. The follow information will be printed on Console.
[P831|Terminal Display] CPU:   MPC8247 (HiP7 Rev 14, Mask 1.0 1K50M) at 350 MHz
Board: 8247 (PCI Agent Mode)
I2C:   ready
DRAM:  256 MB
In:    serial
Out:   serial
Err:   serial
Net:   FCC1 ETHERNET, FCC2 ETHERNET [PRIME]
Press ctrl+b to stop autoboot: 3
[P832|Heading 5] Step 2 Press ctrl+b. stop autoboot.
[P833|Terminal Display] Bootrom#
[P834|Heading 5] Step 3 Under boot loader interface, use the following instructions.
[P835|Terminal Display] Bootrom# boot_flash_nopass
Bootrom# Do you want to  revert  to the default config file ? [Y|N|E]:
[P836|Normal]  Please remember your username and password.
[P837|Body Text] Recovering the password may lead configuration lost or service interrupted; we strongly recommend that user should remember the username and password.
[P838|Heading 3] Application cases
[P839|Normal] N/A
[P840|Heading 2] Configuring FTP
[P841|Heading 3] Overview
[P842|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P843|Normal] You can download a switch configuration file from an FTP server or upload the file from the switch to an FTP server. You download a switch configuration file from a server to upgrade the switch configuration. You can overwrite the current startup configuration file with the new one. You upload a switch configuration file to a server for backup purposes. You can use this uploaded configuration for future downloads to the switch or another switch of the same type.
[P844|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P845|Normal] N/A
[P846|Heading 3] Configuration
[P847|Normal] You can copy configurations files to or from an FTP server. The FTP protocol requires a client to send a remote username and password on each FTP request to a server.
[P848|Body Text] Before you begin downloading or uploading a configuration file by using FTP, do these tasks:
[P849|Item List] Ensure that the switch has a route to the FTP server. The switch and the FTP server must be in the same network if you do not have a router to route traffic between subnets. Check connectivity to the FTP server by using the ping command.
[P850|Item List] If you are accessing the switch through the console or a Telnet session and you do not have a valid username, make sure that the current FTP username is the one that you want to use for the FTP download.
[P851|Item List] When you upload a configuration file to the FTP server, it must be properly configured to accept the write request from the user on the switch.
[P852|Normal] For more information, see the documentation for your FTP server.
[P853|Heading 4] Downloading a configuration file by using FTP in IPv4 network
[P854|Heading 5] step 1 copy the configuration file
[P855|Terminal Display] Switch# copy mgmt-if ftp://test:test@10.10.10.163/ startup-config.conf  flash:/startup-config.conf
[P856|Heading 5] step 2 Validation
[P857|Normal] Use the following command to display the configuration
[P858|Terminal Display] Switch# show startup-config
[P859|Heading 4] Uploading a configuration file by using FTP in IPv4 network
[P860|Heading 5] step 1 copy the configuration file
[P861|Terminal Display] Switch# copy flash:/startup-config.conf mgmt-if ftp://test:test@10.10.10.163/startup-config.conf
[P862|Heading 4] Downloading a configuration file by using FTP in IPv6 network
[P863|Normal] Username and password settings are same as IPv4 network.
[P864|Heading 5] step 1 copy the configuration file

[P866|Heading 4] Uploading a configuration file by using FTP in IPv6 network
[P867|Normal] Username and password settings are same as IPv4 network.
[P868|Heading 5] step 1 copy the configuration file
[P869|Terminal Display] Switch# copy flash:/startup-config.conf mgmt-if ftp://root:root@2001:1000::2 startup-config.conf

[P872|Heading 2] Configuring FTP SERVER
[P873|Heading 3] Overview
[P874|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P875|Normal] You can download a switch configuration file from an FTP server or upload the file from the switch to an FTP server. You download a switch configuration file from a server to upgrade the switch configuration. You can overwrite the current startup configuration file with the new one. You upload a switch configuration file to a server for backup purposes. You can use this uploaded configuration for future downloads to the switch or another switch of the same type.
[P876|Heading 4] Principle Description

[P880|Body Text] Before you begin downloading or uploading a configuration file by using FTP, do these tasks:
[P881|Item List] Ensure that the switch has a route to the FTP server. The switch and the FTP server must be in the same network if you do not have a router to route traffic between subnets. Check connectivity to the FTP server by using the ping command.
[P882|Item List] If you are accessing the switch through the console or a Telnet session and you do not have a valid username, make sure that the current FTP username is the one that you want to use for the FTP download.
[P883|Item List] When you upload a configuration file to the FTP server, it must be properly configured to accept the write request from the user on the switch.

[P905|Heading 2] Configuring TFTP
[P906|Heading 3] Overview
[P907|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P908|Normal] You can download a switch configuration file from a TFTP server or upload the file from the switch to a TFTP server. You download a switch configuration file from a server to upgrade the switch configuration. You can overwrite the current file with the new one. You upload a switch configuration file to a server for backup purposes; this uploaded file can be used for future downloads to the same or another switch of the same type.
[P909|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P910|Normal] N/A
[P911|Heading 3] Configuration
[P912|Normal] Before you begin downloading or uploading a configuration file by using TFTP, do these tasks:
[P913|Body Text] Ensure that the workstation acting as the TFTP server is properly configured.
[P914|Body Text] Ensure that the switch has a route to the TFTP server. The switch and the TFTP server must be in the same network if you do not have a router to route traffic between subnets. Check connectivity to the TFTP server by using the ping command.
[P915|Body Text] Ensure that the configuration to be downloaded is in the correct directory on the TFTP server.
[P916|Body Text] For download operations, ensure that the permissions on the file are set correctly.
[P917|Body Text] During upload operations, if you are overwriting an existing file (including an empty file, if you had to create one) on the server, ensure that the permissions on the file are set correctly.
[P918|Heading 4] Downloading a configuration file by using TFTP in IPv4 network
[P919|Terminal Display] Switch# copy mgmt-if tftp://10.10.10.163/startup-config.conf flash:/startup-config.conf
[P920|Heading 4] Uploading a configuration file by using TFTP in IPv4 network
[P921|Terminal Display] Switch# copy flash:/startup-config.conf mgmt-if tftp://10.10.10.163/startup-config.conf
[P922|Heading 4] Downloading a configuration file by using TFTP in IPv6 network
[P923|Terminal Display] Switch# copy mgmt-if tftp://2001:1000::2/startup-config.conf flash:/startup-config.conf
[P924|Heading 4] Uploading a configuration file by using TFTP in IPv6 network
[P925|Terminal Display] Switch# copy flash:/startup-config.conf mgmt-if tftp://2001:1000::2/startup-config.conf
[P926|Heading 3] Application cases
[P927|Normal] N/A
[P928|Heading 2] Configuring SCP
[P929|Heading 3] Overview
[P930|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P931|Normal] SCP，which is short for secure copy, is a part of SSH protocol. It is a remote copy technology which is based on SSH protocol. User can download a switch configuration file from a SCP server or upload the file from the switch to a SCP server. User can download a switch configuration file from a server to upgrade the switch configuration and overwrite the current file with the new one. User can upload a switch configuration file to a server for backup purposes; this uploaded file can be used for future downloads to the same or another switch of the same type.
[P932|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P933|Normal] N/A
[P934|Heading 3] Configuration
[P935|Normal] Before you begin downloading or uploading a configuration file by using SCP, do these tasks:
[P936|Body Text] Ensure that the workstation acting as the SCP server is properly configured.
[P937|Body Text] Ensure that the switch has a route to the SCP server. The switch and the SCP server must be in the same network if you do not have a router to route traffic between subnets. Check connectivity to the SCP server by using the ping command.
[P938|Body Text] Ensure that the configuration to be downloaded is in the correct directory on the SCP server.
[P939|Body Text] For download operations, ensure that the permissions on the file are set correctly.
[P940|Body Text] During upload operations, if you are overwriting an existing file (including an empty file, if you had to create one) on the server, ensure that the permissions on the file are set correctly.
[P941|Heading 4] Downloading a configuration file by using SCP in IPv4 network
[P942|Terminal Display] Switch# copy mgmt-if scp://10.10.10.163/startup-config.conf flash:/startup-config.conf

[P951|Heading 2] Configuring Telnet
[P952|Heading 3] Overview
[P953|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P954|Normal] Telnet is a network protocol used on the Internet or local area networks to provide a bidirectional interactive text-oriented communications facility using a virtual terminal connection. User data is interspersed in-band with Telnet control information in an 8-bit byte oriented data connection over the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP). Telnet was developed in 1969 beginning with RFC 15, extended in RFC 854, and standardized as Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) Internet Standard STD 8, one of the first Internet standards. Historically, Telnet provided access to a command-line interface (usually, of an operating system) on a remote host. Most network equipment and operating systems with a TCP/IP stack support a Telnet service for remote configuration (including systems based on Windows NT). Because of security issues with Telnet, its use for this purpose has waned in favor of SSH.

[P977|Heading 2] Configuring SSH
[P978|Heading 3] Overview
[P979|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P980|Normal] The Secure Shell (SSH) is a protocol that provides a secure, remote connection to a device. SSH provides more security for remote connections than Telnet does by providing strong encryption when a device is authenticated. SSH supports the Data Encryption Standard (DES) encryption algorithm, the Triple DES (3DES) encryption algorithm, and password-based user authentication. The SSH feature has an SSH server and an SSH integrated client, which are applications that run on the switch. You can use an SSH client to connect to a switch running the SSH server. The SSH server works with the SSH client supported in this release and with SSH clients. The SSH client also works with the SSH server supported in this release and with SSH servers.
[P981|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P982|Normal] N/A

[P993|Heading 5] step 4 Create a private key named a.pub with key a and save it to flash

[P1014|Heading 2] Configuring Time&timezone
[P1015|Heading 3] Overview
[P1016|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1017|Normal] If no other source of time is available, you can manually configure the time and date after the system is restarted. The time remains accurate until the next system restart. We recommend that you use manual configuration only as a last resort. If you have an outside source to which the switch can synchronize, you do not need to manually set the system clock.

[P1032|Heading 2] Configuring License
[P1033|Heading 3] Overview
[P1034|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1035|Normal] License will control the features on the switch; each switch has its own license to avoid the unauthorized user to use the advanced features. There are totally three kinds of licenses: Enterprise Base, Metro Service, and Metro Advanced. Different license will contain different features. Customer can apply different license to satisfy different requirement. If switch has no license, it can only provide L2 features. Different switch can’t share the same license. In order to get the license for the specify switch, first generate the unique device identifier(UDI) for the switch and then send the UDI to vendor to apply the license, at last get the license from vendor and use the license on the switch.
[P1036|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1037|Normal] N/A
[P1038|Heading 3] Configuration
[P1039|Heading 5] step 1 Create UDI for the device and send it to remote FTP server
[P1040|Terminal Display] Switch# generate device identifier mgmt-if ftp://test:test@10.10.25.33/device.udi
[P1041|Heading 5] step 2 Apply license
[P1042|Normal] Send UDI file to vendor, vendor will generate license for customer requirement.
[P1043|Heading 5] step 3 Use license
[P1044|Normal] Get the license to local from remote FTP server, and reload the system.
[P1045|Terminal Display] Switch# copy mgmt-if ftp://test:test@10.10.25.33/device.lic flash:/device.lic
Switch# reload
[P1046|Normal] 
[P1047|Body Text] You must reload the switch for the license to take effect.
[P1048|Body Text] If the switch has no license, it can only work with L2 features.
[P1049|Body Text] If the switch has more than one license, all the features contain by the licenses can take effect

[P1068|Heading 2] RPC API Configuration Guide
[P1069|Heading 3] Overview
[P1070|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1071|Normal] RPC API service allows user to configure and monitor the switch system through Remote Procedure Calls (RPC) from your program.
[P1072|Body Text] The service currently supports JSON-RPC over HTTP protocol together with HTTP Basic authentication.
[P1073|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1074|Normal] RPC API service uses standard JSON-RPC over HTTP protocol to communicate the switch and your program. User may issue switch CLI commands through JSON-RPC method: ‘executeCmds’. By default, the CLI mode is in privileged EXEC mode (#).
[P1075|Body Text] User could send JSON-RPC request via an HTTP POST request to URL: http://:/command-api. The detailed JSON-RPC request and response are show below:
[P1076|Heading 5] JSON-RPC Request
[P1077|Terminal Display] {
    "params":[                                          Parameters for command
        {                                               
            "format":"text",                            Expected response format, can be ‘text’ or ‘json’, 
the default format is ‘text’                            
            "version":1,                                The API version
            "cmds":[                                    List of CLI commands
                "show run",                             CLI command 1
                "config t",                             CLI command 2
                "vlan database",                        CLI command 3
                "vlan 1-8",                             CLI command 4
                "interface eth-0-1",                    CLI command 5
                "switchport mode trunk",                CLI command 6
                "switchport trunk allowed vlan add 2",  CLI command 7
                "shutdown",                             CLI command 8
                "end",                                  CLI command 9
                "show interface switchport"             CLI command 10
            ]                                           
        }                                               
    ],                                                  
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",                                    JSON RPC protocol version. Always 2.0.
    "method":"executeCmds",                             Method to run the switch CLI commands
    "id":"70853aff-af77-420e-8f3c-fa9430733a19"         JSON RPC unique identifier
}
[P1078|Heading 5] JSON-RPC Response
[P1079|Terminal Display] {
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",                                     JSON RPC protocol version. Always 2.0.
    "id":"70853aff-af77-420e-8f3c-fa9430733a19",         JSON RPC unique identifier
    "result":[                                           Result list of objects from each CLI command executed. 
        {                                                
            "sourceDetails":"version 5.1.6.fcs\n!\n …",  Output information of CLI Command 1.
                                                         The Original ASCII output information returned from CLI command if this command is successfully executed.
            "errorCode":-1003,                           Error code if it is available.
            "errorDesc":"unsupported command…",          Error description if it is available.
            "warnings":"% Invalid…",                     Warnings if it is available.
                                                         Formatted JSON object will also be returned if it is available.
        },                                               
        { },                                             Output information of CLI Command 2.
        { },                                             Output information of CLI Command 3.
        { },                                             Output information of CLI Command 4.
        { },                                             Output information of CLI Command 5.
        { },                                             Output information of CLI Command 6.
        { },                                             Output information of CLI Command 7.
        { },                                             Output information of CLI Command 8.
        { },                                             Output information of CLI Command 9.
        {
            "sourceDetails":" Interface name          : eth-0-1\n Switchport mode         : trunk\n …\n"
        }                                                Output information of CLI Command 10.
    ]
}
[P1080|Heading 5] Python Client Example Code
[P1081|Normal] Here is an example code using ‘pyjsonrpc’ library:
[P1082|Terminal Display] import pyjsonrpc
import json

http_client = pyjsonrpc.HttpClient(
    url = "http://10.10.39.64:80/command-api",
    username = "username",
    password = "password"
)

cmds = {}
cmd_list = ["show run", "config t", "vlan database", "vlan 1-8", "interface eth-0-1", "switchport mode trunk", "switchport trunk allowed vlan add 2", "shutdown", "end", "show interface switchport"]

cmds['cmds'] = cmd_list
cmds['format'] = 'text'
cmds['version'] = 1

try:
    response = http_client.call("executeCmds", cmds)
    print("json response:");
    json_result = json.dumps(response, indent=4)
    print(json_result)
except Exception, e:
    if e.code == 401:
        print "Unauthorized user"
    else:
        print e.message
        print e.data
[P1083|Heading 5] Error code
[P1084|Normal] Here is a list of JSON-RPC 2.0 error code:

[TABLE 1] rows=6 cols=2
R1	Error Code	Description
R2	-32700	Parse error
R3	-32600	Invalid Request
R4	-32601	Method not found
R5	-32602	Invalid param
R6	-32603	Internal error

[P1085|Body Text] Here is a list of RPC-API error code:

[TABLE 2] rows=12 cols=2
R1	Error Code	Description
R2	-1000	General error
R3	-2001	JSON RPC API Error: unsupported API version
R4	-2002	JSON RPC API Error: must specify ‘params’ with ‘cmds’ in JSON RPC
R5	-2003	JSON RPC API Error: unsupported command response format
R6	-3001	Command execution failed: timed out
R7	-3002	Command execution failed: unsupported command
R8	-3003	Command execution failed: unauthorized command
R9	-3004	Command execution failed: the string does not match any command in current mode
R10	-3005	Command execution failed: can’t convert to JSON format
R11	-3006	Command execution failed: command list too short
R12	-3007	Command execution failed: command list too long

[P1098|Heading 4] Configuring RPC API service with HTTP Authentication
[P1099|Normal] User could configure the HTTP authentication mode of RPC API service.
[P1100|Body Text] Currently, only HTTP Basic authentication is supported. User will receive status code: 401 (Unauthorized access) if user provides invalid user name or password.
[P1101|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode

[P1103|Heading 5] Step 2 Set the username and password, then enable the rpc-api authentication

Switch(config)# service rpc-api auth-mode basic
[P1105|Normal]  Use the following command to disable authentication:

[P1107|Normal]  HTTP authentication settings of RPC API service will take effect after you restart this service or reboot the system.
[P1108|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode

[P1139|Heading 1] Ethernet Configuration Guide
[P1140|Heading 2] Configuring Interface
[P1141|Heading 3] Overview
[P1142|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1143|Normal] Interface status, speed and duplex are configurable.
[P1144|Body Text] When the interface is configured as “no shutdown”, it can work normally after cable is connected. When the interface is configured as “shutdown”, no matter the cable is connected or not, the interface can not work.
[P1145|Body Text] If the device supports combo ports, user can choose to enable copper or fiber mode. The two modes of one port can not work together at same time. The configuration of speed or duplex at combo ports cannot be effective when combo port is working at fiber mode.
[P1146|Body Text] The rule of physical port name is as following: interface name format is eth-[slot]-[port]; [slot] is 0 for single pizza-box switch; when stacking is enabled, the [slot] number is according to the configuration. The [port] number is begin with 1, and increase from up to down, from left to right. The following figure shows the interface name of the device:
[P1147|Normal] 
[P1148|Figure Description] Interface Name
[P1149|Body Text]  To get more information about the interface type and number， please reference to the product spec.
[P1150|Heading 4] Principle Description

[P1180|Heading 4] Configuring Interface Duplex
[P1181|Normal] There are 3 duplex mode supported on the device:

[P1183|Item List] half mode: the interface can transmit or receive packets at same time.
[P1184|Item List] auto mode: the interface should negotiate with the other side to decide the duplex mode.
[P1185|Normal] User can choose proper duplex mode according to the network state.

[P1217|Heading 2] Configuring Layer3 Interfaces
[P1218|Heading 3] Overview
[P1219|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1220|Normal] 3 types of Layer3 interface are supported:
[P1221|Item List] VLAN interfaces: Logical interface with layer3 features. Connect different VLANs via IP address on the VLAN interface. VLAN interfaces can be created and deleted.
[P1222|Item List] Routed Ports: Ports are physical ports configured to be in Layer 3 mode by using the no switchport in interface configuration command.
[P1223|Item List] Layer 3 Link Aggregation Ports: Link Aggregation interfaces made up of routed ports.
[P1224|Normal] A Layer 3 switch can have an IP address assigned to each routed port and VLAN interface. All Layer 3 interfaces require an IP address to route traffic. This section shows how to configure an interface as a Layer 3 interface and how to assign an IP address to an interface.

[P1253|Heading 2] Configuring Interface Errdisable
[P1254|Heading 3] Overview
[P1255|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1256|Normal] Errdisable is a mechanism to protect the system through shutdown the abnormal interface. If an interface enters errdisable state, there are two ways to recovery it from errdisabled state. The first one is to enable errdisable recovery of this reason before errdisable detection; the interface will be recovered automatically after the configured time. But if errdisable occurred first, then errdisable recovery is enabled, the errdisable will not be recovered automatically. The secondary one is configuring “no shutdown” command on the errdisabled interface.
[P1257|Body Text] The flap of interface link state is a potential error caused by hardware or line problem. The administrator can also configure the detection conditions of interface link flap to suppress the flap.
[P1258|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1259|Heading 6] N/ATerminology and definition
[P1260|Normal] Errdisable Status: Interface which is shutdown by Errdisable feature because of abnormal event, we call this status as “Errdisable status” in this document.
[P1261|Body Text] Errdisable Reason: The abnormal event is called as “Errdisable reason”. The reasons are listed in the following table:
[P1262|Table Description] Errdisable Reason Description 

[TABLE 3] rows=13 cols=2
R1	Name	Explanation
R2	bpduguard	System received a BPDU packet on stp edge port
R3	bpduloop	System received a BPDU packet sent by local device
R4	link-monitor-failure	EFM exceed threshold detected
R5	oam-remote-failure	EFM failure detected
R6	port-security	System received a Packet with trustless MAC address
R7	link-flap	Link Flapping
R8	monitor-link	The uplink port is down， lead related downlink port enter errdisable status
R9	udld	Unidirectional detected
R10	fdb-loop	MAC address flapping
R11	loopback-detection	Network loop back detection
R12	reload-delay	The interface is in reload-delay period. The reload delay period specifies the interval that non-peer links are disabled after an MLAG peer reboots
R13	dual-active-conflict	Dual active conflict in stacking environment detected

[P1263|Heading 3] Configuration

[P1303|Heading 3] FAQ
[P1304|Normal] The following example shows how to analyze the abnormality event fdb-loop and link-flap.
[P1305|Heading 4] fdb-loop
[P1306|Normal] Fdb-loop is also called as MAC address flapping. The switch records the source MAC address，VLAN，received interface into the MAC address table when learning MAC address. If the packets with same VLAN and same MAC address are continuously received from different interfaces, the MAC address table will be updated again and again by MAC learning function. This phenomenon is called fdb-loop (or MAC address flapping). Fdb loop may lead traffic forwarding error or network storm. It is an abnormality of the network.
[P1307|Body Text] Fdb-loop may cause by traffic loop back. The most common reason is BUM traffic cyclic forwarding when there is a loop in the network. The system checks frequency of flapping. If the frequency of flapping exceeds the specific threshold, it will meet the condition of fdb-loop. In the case of Errdisable reason fdb-loop enabled, system will set one of the fdb-loop interface to Errdisable status randomly. Otherwise in the case of Errdisable reason fdb-loop disabled, system only records a log and do nothing else.
[P1308|Body Text] Possible reasons analyze:
[P1309|Item List] It has misconnected network cables and network error form to a ring network, which will lead to MAC address flapping frequently.
[P1310|Item List] There are bunch of virtual machines drifting in the network to form MAC address flapping frequently.
[P1311|Item List] There is illegal traffic in the network, like unauthorized users launch MAC address attack and so on.
[P1312|Item List] There are different physical devices in the network, like testers and physical machines sending traffics that have same source MAC and VLAN.
[P1313|Normal] Errdisable protecting fdb-loop is disabled by default， in order to prevent uplink port down and lead bigger service malfunction. If it is necessary to be enabled, the “errdisable fdb-loop trust” command can be used to protect the important service port such as uplink port which should never be shut down by Errdisable functions.
[P1314|Heading 4] link-flap
[P1315|Normal] Link-flap is defined as interface that converts UP/DOWN status continuously. Link-flap may lead service interrupt. A common scene is the primary link down and the service traffic switch to the backup link. If link flap happened on the primary link, the primary link and the backup link will switch frequently and impact the service. To prevent the instability status, system checks frequency of flapping. If the frequency of flapping exceeds the specific threshold, it will meet the condition of link-flap. In the case of Errdisable reason link-flap enabled, system will set the interface to Errdisable status. Otherwise in the case of Errdisable reason link-flap disabled, system only records a log and do nothing else.
[P1316|Body Text] Link-flap is mainly caused by physical reasons, such as cable/DAC/optical fiber/module issues, wavelength division devices rotating, etc.
[P1317|Body Text] Errdisable protecting link-flap is enabled by default. We do not recommend users to disable it.
[P1318|Heading 2] Configuring MAC Address Table
[P1319|Heading 3] Overview
[P1320|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1321|Normal] MAC address table contains address information for the switch to forward traffic between ports. The address table includes these types of address:
[P1322|Item List] Dynamic address: the source address learnt by the switch and will be aged after aging time if this address is not hit. We only support IVL learning mode.
[P1323|Item List] Static address: the source address manually added by administrators.
[P1324|Normal] Following is a brief description of terms and concepts used to describe the MAC address table:
[P1325|Item List] IVL: Independent VLAN Learning: for a given set of VLANs, if a given individual MAC Address is learned in one VLAN, it can’t be used in forwarding decisions taken for that address relative to any other VLAN in the given set.
[P1326|Item List] SVL: Shared VLAN Learning: for a given set of VLANs, if an individual MAC Address is learned in one VLAN, it can be used in forwarding decisions taken for that address relative to all other VLANs in the given set.
[P1327|Normal] Reference to standard:IEEE 802.1D，IEEE 802.1Q
[P1328|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1329|Normal] N/A
[P1330|Heading 3] Configuration
[P1331|Heading 4] Configuring Address Aging Time
[P1332|Normal] 
[P1333|Figure Description] Mac address aging
[P1334|Body Text] The aging time is not exact time. If aging time set to N, then the dynamic address will be aged after N~2N interval. The default aging time is 300 seconds.
[P1335|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P1336|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P1337|Heading 5] step 2 Set dynamic address aging time
[P1338|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# mac-address-table ageing-time 10
[P1339|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P1340|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P1341|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P1342|Normal] Use the following command to display the aging time:

[P1402|Heading 2] Configuring VLAN
[P1403|Heading 3] Overview
[P1404|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1405|Normal] VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) is a switched network that is logically segmented the network into different broadcast domain so that packets are only switched between ports that are designated for the same VLAN. Each VLAN is considered as a logical network, and packets send to stations that do not belong to the same VLAN must be forwarded through a router.
[P1406|Body Text] Reference to standard: IEEE 802.1Q
[P1407|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1408|Normal] Following is a brief description of terms and concepts used to describe the VLAN:
[P1409|Item List] VID: VLAN identifier
[P1410|Item List] LAN: Local Area Network
[P1411|Item List] VLAN: Virtual LAN
[P1412|Item List] PVID: Port VID, the untagged or priority-tagged frames will be assigned with this VID
[P1413|Normal] Tagged Frame: Tagged Frame is inserted with 4 Bytes VLAN Tag, show in the picture below:
[P1414|Normal] 
[P1415|Figure Description] Tagged Frame
[P1416|Body Text] Trunk Link: Both tagged and untagged frames can be transmitted on this link. Trunk link allow for multiple VLANs to cross this link, show in the picture below:
[P1417|Normal] 
[P1418|Figure Description] Trunk link
[P1419|Body Text] Access Link: Only untagged frames can be transmitted on this link. Access link is at the edge of the network, where end stations attach, show in the picture below:
[P1420|Normal] 
[P1421|Figure Description] Access link
[P1422|Heading 3] Configuration
[P1423|Heading 4] Configuring Access Port
[P1424|Normal] 
[P1425|Figure Description] Access link
[P1426|Body Text] Access port only receives untagged or priority-tagged frames, and transmits untagged frames.

[P1429|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan

Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 2
Switch(config-vlan)# exit

[P1432|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 2

[P1440|Heading 4] Configuring Trunk Port
[P1441|Normal] Trunk port receives tagged, untagged, and priority-tagged frames, and transmits both untagged and tagged frames. If trunk port receives an untagged frame, this frame will be assigned to the VLAN of the trunk port’s PVID; if a frame send out from the trunk port and the frame’s VID is equal to the trunk port’s PVID, this frame will be send out without VLAN tag.
[P1442|Normal] 
[P1443|Figure Description] Trunk link

[P1463|Heading 2] Configuring Voice VLAN
[P1464|Heading 3] Overview
[P1465|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1466|Normal] With the development of the voice technology, the use of IP Phone/IAD(Integrated Access Device) is becoming more and more widespread in broadband community. Voice and data traffics are usually present in the network at the same time, therfore, voice traffics need higher priority to improve the performance and reduce the packet loss rate.
[P1467|Body Text] The traditional method to improve the quality of voice traffic is using ACL to separate the voice packets, and using QoS to ensure the transmit quality.
[P1468|Body Text] The voice VLAN feature can identify the voice packets by source mac, which makes the conguration more convenient.
[P1469|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1470|Normal] N/A
[P1471|Heading 3] Configuration
[P1472|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P1473|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P1474|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan
[P1475|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 2
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P1476|Heading 5] step 3 Set the cos of voice vlan (Optional)
[P1477|Normal] The default cos is 5.
[P1478|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# voice vlan set cos to 7
[P1479|Heading 5] step 4 Set the voice vlan and create a mac entry for it
[P1480|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# voice vlan 2
Switch(config)# voice vlan mac-address 0055.0000.0000 ffff.ff00.0000 description test
[P1481|Heading 5] step 5 Enter the interface configure mode and enable voice vlan
[P1482|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan all
Switch(config-if)# voice vlan enable
Switch(config-if)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan all
[P1483|Heading 5] step 6 Validation
[P1484|Normal] Send packet to eth-0-1, the format of the packet is as below（priority in Vlan tag is 0）：
[P1485|Terminal Display]     0x0000:  0000 0a02 0001 0055 0000 0011 8100 0002  ........k.......
    0x0010:  0800 aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd  ................
    0x0020:  aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd  ................
    0x0030:  aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd            ............
[P1486|Normal] Receive packet from eth-0-2, the format of the packet received is as below（priority in Vlan tag is 5）：.
[P1487|Terminal Display]     0x0000:  0000 0a02 0001 0055 0000 0011 8100 a002  ........k.......
    0x0010:  0800 aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd  ................
    0x0020:  aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd  ................
    0x0030:  aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd aadd            ............

[P1489|Normal] N/A
[P1490|Heading 2] Configuring VLAN Classification
[P1491|Heading 3] Overview
[P1492|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1493|Normal] VLAN classification is used to define specific rules for directing packets to selected VLANs based on protocol or subnet criteria. Sets of rules can be grouped (one group per interface).
[P1494|Body Text] VLAN classification rules have 3 types: mac based, ip based and protocol based. MAC based vlan classification rule will classify packets to specified VLAN according to the source MAC address of incoming packets; IP based vlan classification rule will classify packets according to the source IP address of incoming packets; And protocol based vlan classification rule will classify packets according to the layer3 type of incoming packets. The following layer3 types can be supported: ARP, IP(v4), MPLS, Mcast MPLS, PPPoE, RARP.
[P1495|Body Text] Different types of vlan classification rules can be added to same vlan classification group. VLAN classification group can only be applied on switchport. Only one type of vlan classification rules can take effect on one switchport.
[P1496|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1497|Normal] N/A
[P1498|Heading 3] Configuration
[P1499|Normal] 
[P1500|Figure Description] vlan classification
[P1501|Body Text] In this configuration example, three VLAN classifier rules are created:
[P1502|Body Text] Rule 1 is mac based rule, it will classify the packets with MACSA 2222.2222.2222 to vlan 5;
[P1503|Body Text] Rule 2 is ip based rule, it will classify the packets sourced from IP adress 1.1.1.1/24 to vlan 5;
[P1504|Body Text] Rule 3 is protocol based rule, it will classify all arp packets to vlan 5.
[P1505|Body Text] Add rule 1, rule2, rule3 to group 31. Then apply group 31 to 3 interfaces: eth-0-1, eth-0-2, eth-0-3. These 3 interfaces have different vlan classification type. eth-0-1 is configured to ip based vlan class, this means only ip based rules can take effect on this interface. eth-0-2 is configured to mac based vlan class, this means only mac based rules can take effect on this interface. eth-0-3 is configured to protocol based vlan class, this means only protocol based rules can take effect on this interface.
[P1506|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P1507|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P1508|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan
[P1509|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan database 
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 5 
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 6 
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P1510|Heading 5] step 3 Create vlan classifier rule and add the rules to the group
[P1511|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan classifier rule 1 mac 2222.2222.2222 vlan 5
Switch(config)# vlan classifier rule 2 ip 1.1.1.1 vlan 5
Switch(config)# vlan classifier rule 3 protocol arp vlan 5

Switch(config)# vlan classifier group 31 add rule 1 
Switch(config)# vlan classifier group 31 add rule 2
Switch(config)# vlan classifier group 31 add rule 3
[P1512|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# arp as-layer-3 enable
[P1513|Heading 5] step 4 Apply the vlan classifier group on the interface
[P1514|Normal] interface eth-0-1：
[P1515|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 6
Switch(config-if)# switchport access allowed vlan add 5
Switch(config-if)# vlan classifier activate 31 based ip 
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P1516|Normal] interface eth-0-2：
[P1517|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 6
Switch(config-if)# switchport access allowed vlan add 5
Switch(config-if)# vlan classifier activate 31 based mac
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P1518|Normal] interface eth-0-3：
[P1519|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-3
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 6
Switch(config-if)# switchport access allowed vlan add 5
Switch(config-if)# vlan classifier activate 31 based protocol
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P1520|Normal] interface eth-0-6：
[P1521|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-6
Switch(config)#switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 5
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P1522|Heading 5] step 5 Exit the configure mode
[P1523|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P1524|Heading 5] step 6 Validation
[P1525|Normal] Verify the VLAN classifier rules:
[P1526|Terminal Display] Switch# show vlan classifier rule
vlan classifier rule 1 mac 2222.2222.2222 vlan 5
vlan classifier rule 2 ip 1.1.1.1 vlan 5
vlan classifier rule 3 protocol arp vlan 5
[P1527|Normal] Verify the VLAN classifier group:
[P1528|Terminal Display] Switch# show vlan classifier group
vlan classifier group 31 add rule 1
vlan classifier group 31 add rule 2
vlan classifier group 31 add rule 3
[P1529|Normal] Verify the VLAN classifier interface:
[P1530|Terminal Display] Switch# show vlan classifier interface grou
vlan classifier group 31 on interface eth-0-2, based mac
vlan classifier group 31 on interface eth-0-1, based ip
vlan classifier group 31 on interface eth-0-3, based protocol
[P1531|Heading 3] Application cases
[P1532|Normal] N/A
[P1533|Heading 2] Configuring VLAN Mapping
[P1534|Heading 3] Overview
[P1535|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1536|Normal] Service-provider business customers often have specific requirements for VLAN IDs and the number of VLANs to be supported. The VLAN required by different customers in the same service-provider network might overlap, and traffic of customers through the infrastructure might be mixed. Assigning different VIDs to each customer to mapping their own’s would bring the traffic from different customers separate. Using the VLAN translation feature, service providers can use a series of VLANs to support customers who have their own VLANs. Customer VLAN IDs are translated, and traffic from different customers is segregated within the service-provider infrastructure, even when they appear to be on the same VLAN.
[P1537|Body Text] 802.1Q tunneling expands VLAN space by using a VLAN-in-VLAN hierarchy and tagging the tagged packets, and the maximal VLAN number can reach 4096 × 4096 . Using the 802.1Q tunneling feature, service providers can use a single VLAN to support clients which have multiple VLANs. The ISP usually builds a VLAN model to monitor whole VLAN of backbone network by using GARP or GVRP and accelerate network convergence speed by using STP. Using 802.1Q tunneling as initial solution is right at first, but it can cause expansibility problem as clients increased. Some clients hope to bring their own VLAN ID which will face two problems. Firstly, the first client’s VLAN tag may clash with the other clients. Secondly, the usable tags may be severely limited for the service-provider. The core network will have limits on the 4096 numbers VLAN, if the clients are permitted to use their respective VLAN ID by their own manner.
[P1538|Normal] 
[P1539|Figure Description] QinQ Tunnel
[P1540|Body Text] Using 802.1Q tunneling, the client’s VLAN tag is encapsulated in the public VLAN tag and packets with two tags will traverse on backbone network. The client’s VLAN tag will be shield and only the public VLAN tag will be used to transmit. By separating data stream, the client’s VLAN tag is transmitted transparently and different VLAN tags can be used repeatedly. Therefore, using 802.1Q tunneling expands the available VLAN tags. Two types of 802.1q tunneling are supported: basic 802.1Q tunneling and selective 802.1Q tunneling. Basic 802.1Q tunneling is founded on tagging on ports and all dates will be encapsulated a common VLAN tag of the same port, so this type has great limitations in practical applications. While selective 802.1Q tunneling can separate data stream and encapsulate different VLAN tags base on different data.
[P1541|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1542|Normal] N/A
[P1543|Heading 3] Configuration
[P1544|Heading 4] Configuring VLAN Translation
[P1545|Normal] 
[P1546|Figure Description] vlan mapping
[P1547|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P1548|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P1549|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan
[P1550|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 2,3
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P1551|Heading 5] step 3 Create evc and set dot1q mapped vlan
[P1552|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ethernet evc evc_c1
Switch(config-evc)# dot1q mapped-vlan 2
Switch(config)# ethernet evc evc_c2
Switch(config-evc)# dot1q mapped-vlan 3
[P1553|Heading 5] step 4 Create vlan mapping table and bind the vlan and evc
[P1554|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan mapping table vm
Switch(config-vlan-mapping)# raw-vlan 10 evc evc_c1
Switch(config-vlan-mapping)# raw-vlan 20 evc evc_c2
Switch(config-vlan-mapping)# exit
[P1555|Heading 5] step 5 Enable vlan translation on the interface and apply the vlan mapping table
[P1556|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk vlan-translation
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk vlan-translation mapping table vm
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 2,3

Switch(config-if)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 2,3
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P1557|Heading 5] step 6 Exit the configure mode
[P1558|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P1559|Heading 5] step 7 Validation
[P1560|Normal] Use the following command to display the information of the switch port interface:

Interface name          : eth-0-1

[P1562|Normal] Use the following command to display the information of the vlan mapping table：

Table Name        EVC Name          Mapped VLAN Raw VLAN

vm                evc_c1            2           10

[P1565|Normal] 
[P1566|Figure Description] QinQ Tunnel

[P1568|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P1570|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown

[P1575|Terminal Display] Switch# show interface switchport interface eth-0-1
Interface name           : eth-0-1

[P1576|Heading 4] Configuring 802.1q Tunneling （Selective 802.1Q tunneling, Add one tag for incoming untagged packet.）
[P1577|Normal] 
[P1578|Figure Description] QinQ Tunnel
[P1579|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P1580|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P1581|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan
[P1582|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 2,3,20,30
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P1583|Heading 5] step 3 Create evc and set dot1q mapped vlan
[P1584|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ethernet evc evc_c1
Switch(config-evc)# dot1q mapped-vlan 2
Switch(config)# ethernet evc evc_c2
Switch(config-evc)# dot1q mapped-vlan 3
Switch(config)# ethernet evc evc_c3
Switch(config-evc)# dot1q mapped-vlan 20
Switch(config)# ethernet evc evc_c4
Switch(config-evc)# dot1q mapped-vlan 30
Switch(config-evc)# exit
[P1585|Heading 5] step 4 Create vlan mapping table and bind the vlan and evc

[P1624|Heading 2] Configuring Link Aggregation
[P1625|Heading 3] Overview
[P1626|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P1627|Heading 5] Abbreviation

[TABLE 4] rows=5 cols=2
R1	Abbreviation	Full Name
R2	LACP	Link Aggregation Control Protocol
R3	AGG Group	Aggregation Group
R4	AGG IF	Aggregation Interface
R5	Member IF	Member Interface

[P1628|Heading 5] description
[P1629|Normal] Link Aggregation technique is aggregating multiple physical Ethernet interfaces into one, form into an aggregation group in logical; multiple physical interfaces in the same aggregation group will be seen as one interface logically. Using link aggregation technique can reach the goal of increasing link’s bandwidth by binding multiple physical interfaces into one logical interface without upgrading hardware. At the meanwhile as realizing the increased bandwidth, link aggregation uses backup link mechanism, which can improve the reliabilities between devices effectively.
[P1630|Body Text] Link binding is achieved by interface binding. Multiple ethernet interfaces become an aggregation group. The ethernet interfaces are member interfaces . Each aggregation group corresponding to a logical interface, which is called aggregation interface. The aggregation group and aggregation interface should use same index, for example: aggregation group 1 corresponding to aggregation interface 1.
[P1631|Body Text] Types of Aggregation group/interface:
[P1632|Item List] layer 2 Aggregation group/interface: All member interfaces are layer 2 interface
[P1633|Item List] layer 3 Aggregation group/interface: All member interfaces are layer 3 interface
[P1634|Normal] Modes of link aggregation
[P1635|Body Text] There are two modes of link aggregation. The advantages for each mode are as following:
[P1636|Item List] static aggregation mode: After configured, if the member statues is up, the aggregation interface can enter up statues
[P1637|Item List] dynamic aggregation mode: Use LACP protocol to adapt the interface select/un-select statues according to the locol and remote information.
[P1638|Normal] Aggregation groups with static mode called static aggregation group; Aggregation groups with dynamic mode called dynamic aggregation group
[P1639|Body Text] Status of member interface:
[P1640|Item List] w(waiting): in dynamic aggregation mode, this member can not forward data traffic
[P1641|Item List] s(suspend): in dynamic aggregation mode, this member can not forward data traffic
[P1642|Item List] B(bundle): this member can forward data traffic
[P1643|Item List] D(down/admin down): interface is in down status
[P1644|Normal] The aggregation interface is up when at least one member is in “bundle” status.
[P1645|Heading 5] Background
[P1646|Normal] Current problem
[P1647|Body Text] As the network size continuously extend, users increase higher requirements about the bandwidth and reliability of key link. In traditional technology, it always changes interface boards with higher speed rate or devices that support higher speed rate of interface boards; however, this scheme will have higher cost and it is not flexible.
[P1648|Body Text] Advantages of link aggregation
[P1649|Body Text] Link Aggregation technique is aggregating multiple physical Ethernet interfaces into one, form into an aggregation group in logical; multiple physical interfaces in the same aggregation group will be seen as one interface logically. Using link aggregation technique can reach the goal of increasing link’s bandwidth by binding multiple physical interfaces into one logical interface without upgrading hardware. At the meanwhile as realizing the increased bandwidth, link aggregation uses backup link mechanism, which can improve the reliabilities between devices effectively.
[P1650|Body Text] Advantages of link aggregation:
[P1651|Item List] Increase bandwidth: multiple physical interfaces combine into one interface logically; the bandwidth of aggregative interface is the sum of each member interface’s bandwidth.
[P1652|Item List] Link redundancy protection: when there is a certain link fails, traffic can cut back to another useable member links, to increasing the reliability of link aggregation interface.
[P1653|Item List] Load balancing: within one aggregation group, it can realize that load balancing between member links
[P1654|Body Text] 
[P1655|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P1656|Heading 5] LACP Protocol
[P1657|Normal] 
[P1658|Figure Description] LACPDU Packet
[P1659|Table Description] Fields in packet 

[TABLE 5] rows=29 cols=3
R1	Field	Length	Description
R2	Destination Address	6 Bytes	Destination Address which is a multicast address (01-80-C2-00-00-02)
R3	Source Address	6 Bytes	Source Address, which is the MAC address of the transmiting interface
R4	Length/Type	2 Bytes	Protocal type 0x8809
R5	Subtype	1 Bytes	sub type. 0x01 is LACP packet
R6	Version Number	1 Bytes	Protocol version 0x01
R7	TLV_type	1 Bytes	0x00: Terminator0x01:Actor0x02:Partner0x03:Collector
R8	Actor_Information_Length	1 Bytes	Length of actor field. 20 Bytes
R9	Actor_System_Priority	2 Bytes	Local system priority. Configurable. 32768(0x8000) by default
R10	Actor_System	6 Bytes	System ID, which is same as local MAC address
R11	Actor_key	2 Bytes	Interface Key value, which is generated by interface configuration. It is a key factor for the member to join the aggregation group. The interface configuration include AGG index and whether join the MLAG
R12	Actor_Port_Priority	2 Bytes	Interface system priority. Configurable. 2048(0x800) by default
R13	Actor_Port	2 Bytes	Interface index, according to the switch selected interface
R14	Actor_State	1 Bytes	Local statues information, valid range is 0-7. 0(LACP_Activity): The passive/active statues of the interface’s link control. 0 - Passive, 1 - Active.1(LACP_Timeout): timeout value. 0 - Long timeout, 1- short timeout.2(Aggregation): aggregation capacity of the interface. 1 - True, the interface is integrable. 0 - False, independent link, not integrable.3(Synchronization): if the interface is aggregated. 1 - True, the link is in IN_SYNC statues, the interface is in the correct aggregation group. 0 - False, the link is in OUT_OF_SYNC statues, the interface is not in the correct aggregation group.4(Collecting): 1 - True, receiving enabled on current interface. 0 - False, receiving disabled on current interface. 5(Distributing): 1 - True, transmitting enabled on current interface. 0 - False, transmitting disabled on current interface. 6:Defaulted：1 - True, the partner information used by Actor is from the configured default value. 0 - False, he partner information used by Actor is from the LACPDU packets.7(Expired): 1 - True, Actor RX is timeout. 0 - False, Actor RX is not timeout.
R15	Reserved	3 Bytes	Reserved for debug and extension
R16	Partner_Information_Length	1 Bytes	Partner information length. Partner is the remote system/interface/statues information received by the interface, which is corresponding to actor field. At system initial, the partner field is filled with “0”. After received the remote information, the partner field is updated.
R17	Partner_System_Priority	2 Bytes	The priority of remote system
R18	Partner_System	6 Bytes	The system index of remote system, which is same as the MAC address of remote device
R19	Partner_key	2 Bytes	Remote interface KEY value
R20	Partner_Port_Priority	2 Bytes	The priority of remote interface
R21	Partner_Port	2 Bytes	Remote interface index
R22	Partner_State	1 Bytes	Partner_State
R23	Reserved	2 Bytes	Reserved field
R24	Collector_Information_Length	1 Bytes	Collector information length 0x10
R25	CollectorMaxDelay	2 Bytes	Maximum delay. 0xffff by default
R26	Reserved	12 Bytes	Reserved field
R27	Terminator_Length	1 Bytes	Terminator information length 0x00
R28	Reserved	50 Bytes	Reserved field, which is filled with “0”
R29	FCS	4 Bytes	cyclic redundancy check field

[P1660|Body Text] Dynamic aggregation mode is achieved via LACP protocol. The content of LACP protocol and working mechanism of dynamic aggregation mode are described as following:
[P1661|Body Text] LACP protocol based on standard IEEE802.3ad, is to achieved dynamic link aggregation. The devices running LACP protocol use LACPDU to exchange the information of the link aggregation.
[P1662|Body Text] The member interface of aggregation group can send/receive the LACPDU(Link Aggregation Control Protocol Data Unit) to advice the local information to remote end. After the remote device receive the LACPDU, it compare the information with other members and set the member statues to select/un-select.
[P1663|Body Text] LACP working mode supports ACTIVE/PASSIVE.
[P1664|Body Text] At least one device is ACTIVE mode. Only the device in ACTIVE mode can send LACPDU initiative. The device in PASSIVE mode can reply the LACPDU. If both devices are in PASSIVE mode, no LACPDU can be sent.
[P1665|Body Text] LACP protocol defines priority. Priority supports system priority and interface priority. The smaller number indicates higher priority.
[P1666|Item List] System priority: The device with higher priority can decide the select/un-select statues of interface.
[P1667|Item List] Interface priority: The interface with higher priority can be selected preferential.
[P1668|Heading 5] Link Aggregation
[P1669|Normal] 
[P1670|Figure Description] Link Aggregation
[P1671|Body Text] As it shows in Figure, the following explanation shows the forwarding process of link aggregation:
[P1672|Item List] Switch1’s aggregation interface agg1 dock with Switch2’s aggregation interface agg2, the aggregation link is formed between two switches.
[P1673|Item List] The aggregation interface is seen as an interface logically, when broadcast message forwards, there is only one broadcast on agg1, and then load balancing strategy will decide which physical interface will it forwards through.
[P1674|Item List] After the message gets to agg2, Switch2 learns MAC, the corresponding interface is agg2, rather than the physical interface which receives message.
[P1675|Item List] The aggregation link consists of three physical links in the figure, when the load traffic is extremely ideal, the link bandwidth of Switch1 and Switch2 will be the sum of the three physical links’ bandwidths.
[P1676|Heading 5] Link Redundancy
[P1677|Normal] 
[P1678|Figure Description] Link Redundancy
[P1679|Body Text] As the figure shows, when one link fails between Switch1 and Switch2, as long as other links are normal, then aggregation link can still normally forwarding network traffic; merely, the bandwidth of aggregation link decreases.
[P1680|Heading 5] Load balance
[P1681|Normal] 
[P1682|Figure Description] Load balance
[P1683|Body Text] As the figure shows, the traffic which forwards to agg1 will get away from different physical interfaces, to realize traffic’s load balancing.
[P1684|Body Text] There are four modes of load balancing: Static(default), Dynamic, Round-robin, and resilent.
[P1685|Item List] Static: Hash load balancing mode, is to calculate a Hash value according to the Hash Key of message (the default of Hash Key is message’s Dst-IP, Src-IP, Dst-MAC, Src-MAC and IP-Protocol); different Hash values match to different member link, which will realize the effects of load balancing. If the Hash Key sections of tested traffic are the same, then the Hash values calculated are the same, too. It cannot realize the effect in this situation.
[P1686|Item List] Dynamic: load balancing by flow. If port1 has fewer traffic than port2 and port3, the new flow will distribute to port1. But if multi flows enter the device at same time, these flows may be distributed to same port and lead unbalace.
[P1687|Item List] Round-robin: load balancing in round-robin mode. If the first packet is forwarded to port1, the second packet will forward to port2, the third packet will forward to port3, and so on. The problem is if the latency is different for each link, the packets may get out of order.

[P1688|Item List] Resilient: load balancing by hash. The difference with static modes is: in resilient mode, when there is link failure, system will re-calculate the hash value for the traffic on the failure link and re reload to the normal link.
[P1689|Heading 5] High light functions
[P1690|Normal] Weighted link aggregation
[P1691|Normal] 
[P1692|Figure Description] Weighted link aggregation
[P1693|Body Text] Switch1 and Switch2 are connected by two physical links. These two physical links constitute an aggregation link.
[P1694|Body Text] In some case, the two links have different bandwidth, so the different weight is needed to make sure the bandwidth can used reasonable.
[P1695|Body Text] Based on traditional link aggregation, the weighted link aggregation remove the limitation of member interface type, and it supports to aggregate interfaces with different speed. Using the weight configuration to ensure the traffic distribute to the member reasonable.
[P1696|Body Text] Interface weight configuration is valid for static AGG and LACP.
[P1697|Body Text] Master-slave mode link aggregation
[P1698|Normal] 
[P1699|Figure Description] Master-slave mode link aggregation
[P1700|Body Text] Switch1 and Switch2 connected by aggregation link. To prevent single link failure lead network breaking or congestion, the system need a backup link.
[P1701|Body Text] As the figure shows, there are three physical links between Switch1 and Switch2. Two links are working link and one is backup link. If any of the working link failure occurs, the backup link can transmitting the packets instead of the working link.
[P1702|Body Text] Comparing with traditional link aggregation, Master-slave mode link aggregation has following advantages: in traditional link aggregation, links are the backup for each other, when failure occurs the traffic of the failed link need to distribute to other working links. When the network usage is high (for example,in full speed forwarding case), the packets loss can not be prevented.
[P1703|Body Text] The administrator can configure M working lins and N backup links, to make a reasonable ratio of M:N.
[P1704|Body Text] Master-slave mode link aggregation is only valid for LACP
[P1705|Heading 3] Restrictions and Precautions
[P1706|Heading 4] Interface Property
[P1707|Normal] The aggregation interface is a logical interface, part of the attributes must be same among all interfaces. Therefore, when the member join an aggregation interface, it should follow the following rules:
[P1708|Table Description] Aggregation Conditions 

[TABLE 6] rows=10 cols=2
R1	Attribute	Description
R2	interface	All member interfaces types (layer 2 / layer 3) must be same Layer 2 and layer 3 mixed is not allowedThe VLAN id of layer 2 interface should be same
R3	DHCP	The interface with DHCP relay/DHCP snooping/DHCP server/DHCPv6 relay/DHCPv6 snooping enabled can not join the aggregation interface
R4	Port isolate	The port isolate configuration must be same for each member interface
R5	Private VLAN	The Private VLAN type / public VLAN / Private VLAN must be same for each member interface
R6	Error disable	The Error disable configuration must be same for each member interface and aggregation interface
R7	MTU	The MTU value must be same for each member interface and aggregation interface
R8	EFD	The EFD status (enabled/disabled) must be same for each member interface and aggregation interface
R9	MAC Learning	The MAC Learning status (enabled/disabled) must be same for each member interface and aggregation interface
R10	Port Block	The Port Block configuration must be same for each member interface and aggregation interface

[P1709|Heading 4] Features mutual exclusion
[P1710|Normal] Part of features are not supported on aggregation or member interface. See the following table:
[P1711|Table Description] Mutual exclusion 

[TABLE 7] rows=10 cols=2
R1	Feature	Description
R2	IP Source guard	NOT support on aggregation and member interfaces
R3	IVI	NOT support on aggregation and member interfaces
R4	Loop back detection	NOT support on aggregation and member interfaces
R5	Monitor link	Interface with Monitor link enabled can NOT join the aggregation
R6	G.8031/G.8032/ERPS	Interface with G.8031/G.8032/ERPS enabled can NOT join the aggregation.G.8031/G.8032/ERPS can be enabled on aggregation interface
R7	PBR	Interface with PBR enabled can NOT join the aggregation.PBR can be enabled on aggregation interface
R8	QOS policy map	Interface with QOS policy map enabled can NOT join the aggregation.QOS policy map can be enabled on aggregation interface
R9	Port security	Interface with Port security enabled can NOT join the aggregation.Port security can be enabled on aggregation interface
R10	Voice VLAN	Interface with Voice VLAN enabled can NOT join the aggregation.Voice VLAN can be enabled on aggregation interface

[P1712|Heading 4] Specification limitation
[P1713|Normal] The maximum aggregation group/interface and the maximum member interface per-group are limited according to system resources
[P1714|Body Text] System supports 5 modes for aggregation maximum aggregation group/interface and member interface per-group. After the mode changes, it will teke effect after device reboot.
[P1715|Body Text] The 5 modes are described as following.
[P1716|Table Description] Specification modes 

[TABLE 8] rows=6 cols=2
R1	Mode	Description
R2	group-mode flexible	Default group-mode. Support up to 64 aggregation groups(Group 0 is reserved). Maximum member interface per-group is configurable. Support up to 16 member interfaces by default
R3	group-mode 56	Support up to 56 aggregation groups(Group 0 is reserved).Support up to 16 member interfaces
R4	group-mode 32	Support up to 32 aggregation groups(Group 0 is reserved).Support up to 32 member interfaces
R5	group-mode 16	Support up to 16 aggregation groups(Group 0 is reserved).Support up to 64 member interfaces
R6	group-mode 8	Support up to 8 aggregation groups(Group 0 is reserved).Support up to 128 member interfaces

[P1781|Heading 4] Configuring weighted link aggregation
[P1782|Heading 5] Topology
[P1783|Normal] 
[P1784|Figure Description] weighted link aggregation
[P1785|Heading 5] Configuration Ideas
[P1786|Normal] AS the figure shows， Switch2 and Switch3 are access devices. The uplink device is the aggregation layer Switch1. There are two links with different bandwidth between the access and aggregation devices, which become a weight aggregation link. The interface weight configuration is valid for both static AGG and LACP, the following example shows how to enable weighted link aggregation on LACP .
[P1787|Body Text] In this example, we suppose that the physical bandwidth of eth-0-1 is 1 Gbps, the physical bandwidth of eth-0-25 is 10 Gbps. So we can set the weight of interface eth-0-25 as 10 times of the weight of eth-0-1. The real interface type and bandwidth according to different hardware model, please reference to the product specification.
[P1788|Body Text] The ratio of weight and bandwidth is not mandatory. Users can choose the weight value according the network requirements.
[P1789|Heading 5] Configuration Steps
[P1790|Normal] This chapter shows how to configure Switch1 and Switch2.
[P1791|Body Text] The Switch3 is same as Switch1.
[P1792|Body Text] The configurations of Switch1 and Switch2 are as below:
[P1793|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P1794|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P1795|Heading 5] step 2 Configure the interface
[P1796|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown 
Switch(config-if)# channel-group 1 mode active
Switch(config-if)# exit 
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-25
Switch(config-if)# channel-group 1 mode active
Switch(config-if)# distribute-weight 10
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown 
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P1797|Normal] By default, the weight of member interfaces are 1.
[P1798|Body Text] System can only support member weight for static load balance and non self-healing mode. The total weight of all members should not exceed the maximum member count.
[P1799|Heading 5] step 3 Validation

[P1804|Heading 4] Configuring Master-slave mode link aggregation
[P1805|Heading 5] Topology
[P1806|Normal] 
[P1807|Figure Description] Master-slave mode link aggregation
[P1808|Heading 5] Configuration Ideas
[P1809|Normal] AS the figure shows， Switch2 and Switch3 are access devices. The uplink device is the aggregation layer Switch1. The uplink of the access device need large bandwidth to satisfy multi-clients requirements. It also need redundancy link to prevent uplink failure leading all downlink clients out of service.
[P1810|Body Text] In this example, 2:1 backup is configured, which means two working links and one backup link in the network.
[P1811|Heading 5] Configuration Steps
[P1812|Normal] This chapter shows how to configure Switch1 and Switch2.
[P1813|Body Text] The Switch3 is same as Switch1.
[P1814|Body Text] The configurations of Switch1 and Switch2 are as below:
[P1815|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P1816|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P1817|Heading 5] step 2 Configure the interface
[P1818|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown 
Switch(config-if)# channel-group 1 mode active
Switch(config-if)# exit 
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# channel-group 1 mode active
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown 
Switch(config-if)# exit 
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-3
Switch(config-if)# channel-group 1 mode active
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown 
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P1819|Heading 5] step 3 Configure the interface
[P1820|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface agg 1
Switch(config-if)# lacp max-active-linknumber 2
Switch(config-if)# lacp preempt enable 
Switch(config-if)# lacp preempt delay 20
Switch(config-if)# end
[P1821|Normal]  “lacp max-active-linknumber 2” specifies at most two links in working statues. There is one link in backup statues because we have three members. When any of the working links failed, the backup link can become working link.
[P1822|Body Text] “lacp preempt enable” enables preempt. “lacp preempt delay 20” means the link start to preempt working link after 20 seconds. In this case after the previous working link recoverd, it wait for 20 seconds to preempt and become working link again. “preempt delay” can prevent link switch too often when link flaps. The default preempt delay value is 30. If all link has same parameter, the preempt feature can be disabled. By default the preempt feature is disabled.
