[P4551|Heading 2] ConfiguringGlobal ACL
[P4552|Heading 3] Overview
[P4553|Heading 4] Brief Introduction
[P4554|Normal] System will support the configurations of global acl, when port acl, vlan/vlanif acl and global acl existed at the same time, the priority is port acl > vlan/vlanif acl> global acl.
[P4555|Body Text] The specific performance is: When the device receives or sends packets, the system will find the acl rule by the priority, once the rule has hit, the packets will forward immediately. If the upper acl has not hit, then it will research the next acl.
[P4556|Heading 3] Configuration Examples
[P4557|Heading 4] Global ACL Configuration
[P4558|Step] Enter the configure mode
[P4559|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P4560|Step] Enable Global ACL and take affect until the next reload
[P4561|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# global-acl enable
[P4562|Step] Apply the policy to global acl
[P4563|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# service-policy global input pmap
[P4564|Step] Apply the access group to global acl
[P4565|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# access-group global input aaa
[P4566|Step] Validation
[P4567|Terminal Display] DUT1# show running-config  
global-acl enable
service-policy global input pmap
access-group global input aaa
[P4568|Normal] 
[P4569|Heading 1] Device Management Configuration Guide
[P4570|Heading 2] Configuring STM
[P4571|Heading 3] Overview
[P4572|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P4573|Normal] Switch Table Management (STM) is used to configure system resources in the switch to optimize support for specific features, depending on how the switch is used in the network.
[P4574|Body Text] You can select a profile to provide maximum system usage for some functions; for example, use the default profile to balance resources and use vlan profile to obtain max MAC entries.
[P4575|Body Text] To allocate ternary content addressable memory (TCAM) resources for different usages, the switch STM profile prioritize system resources to optimize support for certain features. You can select STM templates to optimize these features:
[P4576|Item List] layer2: The VLAN template supports the maximum number of unicast MAC addresses. It would typically be selected for a Layer 2 switch.
[P4577|Item List] layer3: The routing template maximizes system resources for unicast routing, typically required for a router or aggregator in the center of a network.
[P4578|Item List] ipv6: The ipv6 template，support the ipv6 functions.
[P4579|Item List] mpls: The mpls template supports the maximum number of MPLS/MAC entries.
[P4580|Item List] default: The default template gives balance to all functions.
[P4581|Normal] When users configured a profile mode which is not exist in the next reboot image, then default hardware configure will be used when system up with the next image. The hardware configure may be different from the default profile.
[P4582|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P4583|Normal] N/A
[P4584|Heading 3] Configuration
[P4585|Normal] Follow these guidelines when selecting and configuring STM profiles.
[P4586|Body Text] You must reload the switch for the configuration to take effect.
[P4587|Body Text] Use the “stm prefer layer2” global configuration command only on switches intended for Layer 2 switching with no routing.
[P4588|Body Text] Do not use the layer3 profile if you do not have routing enabled on your switch. The stm prefer layer3 global configuration command prevents other features from using the memory allocated to IPv4 unicast routing in the routing profile.
[P4589|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P4590|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P4591|Heading 5] step 2 Set STM profile(use layer3 for example)
[P4592|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# stm prefer layer3
[P4593|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P4594|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P4595|Heading 5] step 4 Validation

[P4602|Heading 2] Configuring syslog
[P4603|Heading 3] Overview
[P4604|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P4605|Normal] The system message logging software can save messages in a log file or direct the messages to other devices. The system message logging facility has these features:
[P4606|Item List] Provides you with logging information for monitoring and troubleshooting.
[P4607|Item List] Allows you to select the types of logging information that is captured.
[P4608|Item List] Allows you to select the destination of the captured logging information.
[P4609|Normal] By default, the switch logs normal but significant system messages to its internal buffer and sends these messages to the system console. You can specify which system messages should be saved based on the type of the severity level. The messages are time-stamped to enhance real-time debugging and management.
[P4610|Body Text] You can access the logged system messages using the switch command-line interface (CLI) or by saving them to a properly configured log server. The switch software saves the log messages in an internal buffer that can store up to 1000 messages. You can monitor the system messages remotely by accessing the switch through Telnet or the console port, or by viewing the logs on a log server.
[P4611|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P4612|Normal] Terminology:

[P4643|Heading 2] Configuring mirror
[P4644|Heading 3] Overview
[P4645|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P4646|Normal] Mirror function can send one or more copies of packets which are passing through the ports/vlans or sending and receiving by CPU to one or more specified destination ports. It can also send the copies to the CPU and keep in memory or flash files.
[P4647|Body Text] The copies of the packets are used for network analyze. The mirror function does not affect the original network traffic.
[P4648|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P4649|Normal] The following describes concepts and terminology associated with mirror configuration:
[P4650|Normal] 
[P4651|Figure Description] Mirror
[P4652|Heading 5] 1.Mirror session
[P4653|Normal] A mirror session is an association of a mirror destination with one or more mirror source. The mirror destination and mirror source will describe later.
[P4654|Body Text] The device supports up to 3 mirror sessions.
[P4655|Body Text] Mirror sessions do not interfere with the normal operation of the switch. However, an oversubscribed mirror destination, for example, a 10-Gbps port monitoring a 100-Gbps port, results in dropped or lost packets.
[P4656|Heading 5] 2.Mirror direction
[P4657|Normal] The device supports to set the direction of the mirror source, there are 3 options for choose: TX/RX/BOTH.
[P4658|Body Text] Receive (RX) mirror: The goal of receive (or ingress) mirror is to monitor as much as possible packets received by the source interface or VLAN before any modification or processing is performed by the switch. A copy of each packet received (except these packets: BPDU, LACPDU, BMGPDU, packets have been discarded by IP-MAC binding check for Vlan_based mirror, CRC error packets for both Port_based and vlan_based mirror) by the source is sent to the destination port for that mirror session. You can monitor a series or range of ingress ports or VLANs in a mirror session. Packets that are modified because of routing are copied without modification; that is, the original packet is copied. Packets that are modified because of quality of service (QoS)—for example, modified Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP)—are copied with modification. Packets that are modified because of VLAN translation or VLAN classification is copied with the modification. Some features that can cause a packet to be dropped during receive processing have no effect on mirror, the destination port can receive a copy of the packet even if the actual incoming packet is dropped. These features include ingress ACL, VLAN’s ingress filter, MAC filter, STP, VLAN tag control, port security, unknown routing packets.
[P4659|Body Text] Transmit (TX) mirror: The goal of transmit (or egress) mirror is to monitor as much as possible packets sent by the source interface after all modification and processing is performed by the switch. A copy of each packet (except these packets: packets from CPU port for Vlan_based mirror, mirroring packets for both Port_based and vlan_based mirror) sent by the source is sent to the destination port for that mirror session. Some features that can cause a packet to be dropped during transmit processing might have affect on mirror.
[P4660|Body Text] Both: In a mirror session, you can monitor a single port for both received and sent packets.
[P4661|Heading 5] 3.Mirror source
[P4662|Normal] The Mirror source is the original traffic of the network. The types of source are described as following:
[P4663|Body Text] Source port: A source port is a layer2 or layer 2 interface which need to be monitored. A physical port or link agg port can be a source port. The member of link agg port is not supported to be a mirror source.
[P4664|Body Text] Source VLAN: A source vlan is a vlan which need to be monitored. User should create a vlan interface before set a vlan as mirror source.
[P4665|Body Text] CPU:User can set CPU as mirror source to monitor the packets send to or receive from the CPU. The copies of packets send to the mirror destination are before cpu-traffic-limit process. Only session 1 support CPU as mirror source currently.
[P4666|Heading 5] 4.Mirror destination
[P4667|Normal] Mirror function will copy the packets and sent the copies to the mirror destination.
[P4668|Body Text] The types of destination are described as following:
[P4669|Body Text] Local destination port: The destination port should be a physical port or link agg port, member of link agg port is not supported. The destination port has these characteristics:
[P4670|Item List] It must reside on the same switch as the source port.
[P4671|Item List] It should not be in “shutdown” state
[P4672|Item List] It can participate in only one mirror session at a time (a destination port in one mirror session cannot be a destination port for a second mirror session).
[P4673|Item List] It cannot be a source port.
[P4674|Item List] The port does not transmit any traffic except that required for the mirror session.
[P4675|Item List] It does not participate in spanning tree while the mirror session is active.
[P4676|Item List] When it is a destination port, all other normal system function of this port should not work until mirror destination configure disabled on this port.
[P4677|Item List] No address learning occurs on the destination port.
[P4678|Item List] The real statues of the speed/duplex might not coincide with the values which are displayed.
[P4679|Normal] Multi-destination: The device supports to use a group of destination ports to receive several copies of the traffic. The characteristics of each member in the group of destination ports are same as single destination port.
[P4680|Body Text] Remote destination：A remote mirror destination is a remote destination vlan, which has a specified out-going port. The copies of the packets should send to the specified port and add the tag of the remote vlan. A remote destination has these characteristics:
[P4681|Item List] It is a vlan with a specified out going port.
[P4682|Item List] The remote VLAN range should be 2 to 4094. If the VLAN isn’t created in system, user can not configure this VLAN as mirror remote vlan.
[P4683|Item List] The out going port should be a physical port. User should manually check if the out going port can transfer mirrored packets.
[P4684|Item List] Monitor traffic packets are inserted a tag with the remote VLAN ID and directed over the specified out going port to the mirror destination session device.
[P4685|Item List] It is recommended to configure remote mirror’s destination port as switch port. Users should add the destination port to the remote vlan otherwise the mirrored packet can not be transmitted out.
[P4686|Normal] CPU destination：send the copies of packet to the CPU of current device. If there is no analyzer available, user can use CPU as mirror destination and save the result for user or developers analyze packets.
[P4687|Body Text] You can analyze network traffic passing through ports or vlans by using mirror function to send a copy of the traffic to another port on the switch that has been connected to a Switch Probe device or other Remote Monitoring (RMON) probe or security device. However, when there is no other monitoring device for capturing packets, normal mirror destination to ports doesn’t work. So we can set CPU as mirror destination to send a copy of the traffic to CPU for storing packets. It supports the cli to display the packets of mirror CPU and write the packets in a text file. It is a very functional debug tool. Mirror does not affect the switching of network traffic on source ports or source vlans; a copy of the packets received or sent by the source interfaces are sent to the destination CPU. The cpu-traffic-limit rate can be configured. CPU can participate as a destination in only one mirror session.

[P4746|Heading 4] Configuring Remote Mirror
[P4747|Normal] 
[P4748|Figure Description] Remote Mirror
[P4749|Body Text] If local device cannot connect to an analyzer directly, User can choose remote mirror to send the copies of packets with specified vlan tag.
[P4750|Body Text] The remote device can pick out the packets with this vlan for analyze.
[P4751|Body Text] The following example copies the packets form Switch1’s eth-0-1, and send them to Switch2 via Switch1’s eth-0-2. Switch2 sends these packets to the analyzer.
[P4752|Body Text] The configuration of Switch1:
[P4753|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P4754|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P4755|Heading 5] step 2 Set the destination of mirror
[P4756|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 15
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 15
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# monitor session 1 destination remote vlan 15 interface eth-0-2
[P4757|Heading 5] step 3 Set the source of mirror
[P4758|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config)# monitor session 1 source interface eth-0-1 both
[P4759|Heading 5] step 4 Exit the configure mode
[P4760|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P4761|Heading 5] step 5 Validation
[P4762|Terminal Display] SwitchA# show monitor session 1
Session   1
----------
Status             : Valid
Type                :  Remote Session
Source Ports       :
  Receive Only     : 
  Transmit Only    : 
  Both               : eth-0-1
Source VLANs       :
  Receive Only     :   
  Transmit Only    : 
  Both               : 
Destination Port   : eth-0-2
Destination remote VLAN : 15
[P4763|Normal] The configuration of Switch2:
[P4764|Body Text] Use these methods on Switch2 to send packets to analyzer via eth-0-2
[P4765|Heading 5] method 1: use vlan 15 as mirror source，eth-0-2 as mirror destination
[P4766|Terminal Display] Switch # configure terminal
Switch (config)# vlan database
Switch (config-vlan)# vlan 15
Switch (config-vlan)# exit

Switch (config)# interface vlan15
Switch (config-if)# exit

Switch (config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch (config-if)# no shutdown

Switch (config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch (config-if)# no shutdown
Switch (config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch (config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 15
Switch (config-if)# exit

Switch (config)# monitor session 1 destination interface eth-0-2
Switch (config)# monitor session 1 source vlan 15 rx
Switch (config)# end
[P4767|Heading 5] method 2: add both ports in to the same vlan (15), and make the packet flood in this vlan
[P4768|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

Switch(config)# no spanning-tree enable

Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 15
Switch(config-vlan)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 15

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 15
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P4769|Normal] In this configuration vlan tag is stripped because eth-0-2 is access port.
[P4770|Heading 5] method 3: flood in vlan and keep vlan tag 15
[P4771|Normal] If user needs to keep the vlan tag 15, eth-0-2 should be trunk port: (other configurations are same as method 2)
[P4772|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 15
[P4773|Heading 4] Configuring CPU Mirror Dest
[P4774|Normal] 
[P4775|Figure Description] Mirror to cpu
[P4776|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P4777|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P4778|Heading 5] step 2 Set the destination of mirror
[P4779|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# monitor session 1 destination cpu
[P4780|Normal] Set the buffer size and to cpu rate:
[P4781|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# monitor cpu set packet buffer 100
Switch(config)# cpu-traffic-limit reason mirror-to-cpu rate 128
[P4782|Heading 5] step 3 Set the source of mirror
[P4783|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# monitor session 1 source interface eth-0-1 both
[P4784|Heading 5] step 4 Exit the configure mode
[P4785|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P4786|Heading 5] Optional steps
[P4787|Normal] Enable or disable to write the packets in to the flash files.
[P4788|Terminal Display] Switch#  monitor cpu capture packet start
Switch#  monitor cpu capture packet stop
[P4789|Normal] Exchange the files from *.txt to *.pcap
[P4790|Terminal Display] Switch# pcap convert flash:/mirror/MirCpuPkt-2016-02-05-18-31-13.txt flash:/MirCpuPkt-2016-02-05.pcap
[P4791|Normal] Set the action after the packet buffer is exceeded: “drop” means discard the latest packet; “replace” means discard the oldest packet.
[P4792|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# monitor cpu capture strategy drop
Switch(config)# monitor cpu capture strategy replace

[P4810|Heading 2] Configuring Device Management
[P4811|Heading 3] Overview
[P4812|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P4813|Normal] User can manage the switch through the management port. The switch has two management ports: an Ethernet port and a console port.
[P4814|Heading 3] Configuration
[P4815|Heading 4] Configuring console port for management
[P4816|Normal] The default console parameters of switch are:
[P4817|Item List] Baud rate default is 115200.
[P4818|Item List] Data bits default is 8.
[P4819|Item List] Stop bits default is 1.
[P4820|Item List] Parity settings default is none.
[P4821|Normal] Before you can assign switch information, make sure you have connected a PC or terminal to the console port, and configured the PC or terminal software parameters to match the default console port parameters. After login in the switch, you can modify the console parameters.
[P4822|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P4823|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P4824|Heading 5] step 2 Enter line configuration mode and set the console speed
[P4825|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# line console 0
Switch(config-line)# speed 19200
[P4826|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P4827|Terminal Display] Switch(config-line)# end
[P4828|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P4829|Normal] After the above setting, console port parameter has been changed, and the PC or terminal can’t configure the switch by console port. You must update PC or terminal console speed from 115200 to 19200 to match the new console parameter and can continue configure the switch by console port.
[P4830|Heading 4] Configuring out band Ethernet port for management
[P4831|Normal] In order to manage device by out band Ethernet port, you should configure management ip address first by console port.
[P4832|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P4833|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P4834|Heading 5] step 2 Configure switch management address
[P4835|Normal] IPv4 & IPv6 are both supported, for example:
[P4836|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# management ip address 10.10.38.106/24
Switch(config)# management ipv6 address 2001:1000::1/96
[P4837|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P4838|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P4839|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P4840|Terminal Display] Switch# show management ip address 
  Management IP address is:  10.10.38.106/24
  Gateway: 0.0.0.0

Switch # show management ipv6 address

  Gateway: ::
[P4841|Heading 4] Configuring Temperature
[P4842|Normal] The switch supports temperature alarm management. You can configure three temperature thresholds: low, high and critical. When switch temperature is lower than low threshold or higher than higher threshold, the switch will be alarm. If the switch temperature is higher than critical threshold, the switch will cut off its power automatically.
[P4843|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P4844|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P4845|Heading 5] step 2 Configuring temperature threshold
[P4846|Normal] 5℃ for low; 70℃ for high; 90℃ for critical.
[P4847|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# temperature 5 70 90
[P4848|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P4849|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P4850|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P4851|Terminal Display] Switch# show environment
---------------------------------------------------------
Sensor status (Degree Centigrade):
Index Temperature  Lower_alarm  Upper_alarm Critical_limit
1     50           5            70          90
[P4852|Heading 4] Configuring Fan
[P4853|Normal] The switch supports to manage fan automatically. If the fan is fail or the fan tray is absent, the switch will be alarm. And if the fan tray supports speed-adjust, the switch can adjust the fan speed depending on the real-time temperature. The switch has three temperature thresholds: Tlow=50, Thigh=65 and Tcrit=80 Celsius scales. If Temperature<Tlow, the fan will stall; if Tlow<=Temperature<Thigh, the fan will run on 30% speed rate; if Thigh<=Temperature<Tcrit, the fan will run on 70% speed rate; if Tcrit>=Temperature, the fan will run on 100% speed rate. And there has a temperature hysteresis Thyst=2 Celsius scales. Assuming temperature has previously crossed above Tlow, Thigh or Tcrit, then the temperature must drop below the points corresponding Thyst(Tlow-Thyst, Thigh-Thyst or Tcrit-Thyst) in order for the condition to drive fan speed rate to lower level. For example:
[P4854|Item List] temperature is 58 Celsius scales, the fan speed rate is 30%; (Tlow<58<Thigh)
[P4855|Item List] temperature increases to 65 Celsius scales, the fan speed rate is 70%;(Thigh=65)
[P4856|Item List] temperature decreases to 63 Celsius scales, the fan speed rate is still 70%;(Thigh-Thyst =63)
[P4857|Item List] temperature decreases to 62 Celsius scales, the fan speed rate is 30%;(62<Thigh-Thyst)
[P4858|Normal] The Tlow, Thigh, Tcrit, Thyst and fan speed rate for each temperature threshold are hard code, and couldn’t be modified.

1-2        OK      30%      Auto

[P4864|Heading 4] Configuring Transceiver
[P4865|Normal] The switch supports manage the transceiver information, and the transceiver information includes basic information and diagnostic information. The basic information includes transceiver type, vendor name, PN, S/N, wavelength and link length for supported type. The diagnostic information includes real-time temperature, voltage, current, optical transmit power, optical receive power and the threshold about these parameters. If the transceiver is inserted or removed, the real-time parameter is out of threshold, the switch will notice the users.

[P4898|Heading 2] Configuring Bootrom
[P4899|Heading 3] Overview
[P4900|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P4901|Normal] The main function of Bootrom is to initialize the board simply and load the system image to boot. You can use some necessary commands in bootrom mode.
[P4902|Body Text] Bootrom can load the system image both from TFTP server and persistent storage like flash. Then you can configure the Switch and TFTP server IP address as environment variables in Bootrom mode for boot the system image.
[P4903|Heading 3] Configuration

bootrom:> reset
[P4908|Heading 5] Method 2: Method 1:Boot the system from TFTP server without password
[P4909|Normal] Save the configuration and reboot the system:

[P4912|Terminal Display] bootrom:> boot_tftp OS-ms-v3.1.9.it.r.bin

[P4954|Heading 2] Configuring SmartConfig
[P4955|Heading 3] Overview
[P4956|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P4957|Normal] SmartConfig is a smart method of switch initial configuration. After enabling SmartConfig, switch will start to download configuration file or image file from tftp server ，if not finding startup-config file at startup. Then switch will install these file ，and it will reboot itself if had downloaded image file.
[P4958|Body Text] Note that we use deploy file to control the configuration file and image file downloaded by switch. Switch fetch these file according the deploy file, which is a XML-formatted file. The deploy file named smartdeploy.xml , while its content like below:
[P4959|Terminal Display] <SmartDeploy>
<ftype>init</ftype>
<hostprefix>Bruce</hostprefix>
<defItem>
<option>enable</option>
<image>def.bin</image>
<config>def.cfg</config>
</defItem>
<groups>
<Item>
<type>MAC</type> 
<value>001e.0808.9100</value> 
<image>switchOs.bin</image>
<config>startup.cfg</config>
</Item>
<Item>
<type>productid</type>
<value>09SWITCH-E48-10</value>
<image>productid.bin</image>
<config>productid.cfg</config>
</Item>
<Item>
<type>SN</type>
<value>E054GD116004</value>
<image>sn.bin</image>
<config>sn.cfg</config>
</Item>
</groups>
</SmartDeploy>
[P4960|Normal] There are three kind of item used by switch to find out image file and configuration file fit itself. Switch will search fit item according sequence like MAC, SN , product-id。We just specify the file name in the deploy file, and place all these file on tftp server.
[P4961|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P4962|Normal] N/A
[P4963|Heading 3] Configuration
[P4964|Normal] 
[P4965|Figure Description] smart config
[P4966|Body Text] This figure is the network topology of testing SmartConfig function，We need two switches and two linux boxes to construct the test bed。”switch” in the figure is the switch we enable SmartCofng on. Note that the address of TFTP server provided by DHCP server can be used by switch to connect to TFTP server directly or via routes.
[P4967|Heading 4] Enable smartConfig
[P4968|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P4969|Terminal Display] Switch#configure terminal
[P4970|Heading 5] step 2 Enable smartConfige
[P4971|Terminal Display] Switch(config)#smart-config initial-switch-deployment
[P4972|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P4973|Terminal Display] Switch (config)#exit
[P4974|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P4975|Normal] Use this command to check the smart-config settings:
[P4976|Terminal Display] Switch# show smart-config config 
Smart-Config config: 
 initial-switch-deployment: on
 hostname-prefix: on
 Send log message to console: on
[P4977|Heading 4] Using smartConfig
[P4978|Normal] SmartConfig was enable default，so we just make sure there is no startup-config.conf file. Then switch will start SmartConfig next boot. And we can delete startup-config.conf manually, so that Smartconfig will work after reboot. Procedure of configure SmartConfig as fallow：
[P4979|Heading 5] step 1:
[P4980|Normal] Configure smartdeploy.xml file，and place it with image file，configuration file to tftp server. The directory must be like this (Configuration files should be in conf directory and images should be in images directory.) ：
[P4981|Terminal Display] smartconfig/
    |--conf/
    |--images/
    |--smartdeploy.xml
[P4982|Heading 5] step 2:
[P4983|Normal] Configure DHCP server，tftp server address option must be set；
[P4984|Heading 5] step 3:
[P4985|Normal] Make sure there is no startup-config.conf file;
[P4986|Heading 5] step 4:
[P4987|Normal] boot or reboot the system.

[P5001|Heading 1] Network Management Configuration Guide
[P5002|Heading 2] Configuring Network Diagnosis
[P5003|Heading 3] Overview
[P5004|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5005|Normal] Ping is a computer network administration utility used to test the reachability of a host on an Internet Protocol (IP) network and to measure the round-trip time for messages sent from the originating host to a destination computer. The name comes from active sonar terminology.
[P5006|Body Text] Ping operates by sending Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) echo request packets to the target host and waiting for an ICMP response. In the process it measures the time from transmission to reception (round-trip time) [1] and records any packet loss. The results of the test are printed in form of a statistical summary of the response packets received, including the minimum, maximum, and the mean round-trip times, and sometimes the standard deviation of the mean.
[P5007|Body Text] Traceroute is a computer network tool for measuring the route path and transit times of packets across an Internet Protocol (IP) network.
[P5008|Body Text] Traceroute sends a sequence of Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) packets addressed to a destination host. Tracing the intermediate routers traversed involves control of the time-to-live (TTL) Internet Protocol parameter. Routers decrement this parameter and discard a packet when the TTL value has reached zero, returning an ICMP error message (ICMP Time Exceeded) to the sender.
[P5009|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5010|Normal] N/A

Switch# traceroute ipv6 2001:1000::1

[P5025|Heading 2] Configuring NTP
[P5026|Heading 3] Overview
[P5027|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5028|Normal] NTP is a tiered time distribution system with redundancy capability. NTP measures delays within the network and within the algorithms on the machine on which it is running. Using these tools and techniques, it is able to synchronize clocks to within milliseconds of each other when connected on a Local Area Network and within hundreds of milliseconds of each other when connected to a Wide Area Network. The tiered nature of the NTP time distribution tree enables a user to choose the accuracy needed by selecting a level (stratum) within the tree for machine placement. A time server placed higher in the tree (lower stratum number), provides a higher likelihood of agreement with the UTC time standard.
[P5029|Body Text] Some of the hosts act as time servers, that is, they provide what they believe is the correct time to other hosts. Other hosts act as clients, that is, they find out what time it is by querying a time server. Some hosts act as both clients and time servers, because these hosts are links in a chain over which the correct time is forwarded from one host to the next. As part of this chain, a host acts first as a client to get the correct time from another host that is a time server. It then turns around and functions as a time server when other hosts, acting as clients, send requests to it for the correct time.
[P5030|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5031|Normal] N/A
[P5032|Heading 3] Configuration
[P5033|Heading 4] Configuring Client/Server mode connecting with in-band interface
[P5034|Normal] Before configuring NTP client, make sure that NTP service is enabled on Server.
[P5035|Normal] 
[P5036|Figure Description] NTP
[P5037|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode

[P5075|Heading 2] ConfiguringPTP
[P5076|Heading 3] Overview
[P5077|Heading 4] Brief Introduction
[P5078|Normal] PTP (Precision Time Protocol) is a protocol for synchronizing computer clocks, defined by the IEEE 1588 standard. PTP aims to accurately synchronize clocks in distributed systems over a network to achieve high-precision time stamps and time synchronization, and is commonly used in industrial automation, transportation, power systems, and other fields that require high-precision time synchronization.
[P5079|Body Text] The PTP protocol is based on a master-slave architecture, where one device acts as the master clock and the rest act as slave clocks. The master clock is the time source in the network, and it synchronizes the clocks of all devices by transmitting time stamps to the slave clocks. The PTP protocol mainly consists of the following important components and steps:
[P5080|Item List] Synchronization process: The master clock publishes time information in the network. After receiving the time information, the slave clock adjusts its local clock to the time of the master clock.
[P5081|Item List] ransmission delay measurement: The master clock measures the propagation delay of its own time information to the slave clock, so that the slave clock can correct its own time.
[P5082|Item List] Time offset calculation: The clock calculates the offset between its own time and the master clock time based on the time information from the master clock and the local time information it receives.
[P5083|Item List] Time correction: Adjust the local time based on the calculated offset from the clock to keep the local time consistent with the master clock time.
[P5084|Normal] The PTP protocol includes two versions: 1588 and G.8275.1. The 1588 includes 1588v1 and 1588v2. 1588v1 can only achieve sub-millisecond time synchronization accuracy, while 1588v2 can achieve sub-microsecond synchronization accuracy. G.8275.1 standard is a precise time synchronization standard defined by ITUT, which is similar to IEEE 1588 standard, both of which are designed to solve the problem of time synchronization across the entire network.
[P5085|Body Text] In wireless networks, clock synchronization between the mobile bearer network and the base station is required. 1588v2 can achieve sub-microsecond time synchronization accuracy with hardware-assisted processing; at the same time, it has lower costs and reduces dependence on GPS.
[P5086|Heading 4] Background
[P5087|Normal] PTP (Precision Time Protocol) is a protocol used to synchronize computer clocks, defined by the IEEE 1588 standard. The background of PTP lies in the need for high-precision time synchronization in various fields, such as industrial automation, transportation, power systems, and other applications where precise time coordination among distributed devices is essential.
[P5088|Body Text] The problem that PTP solves is to provide a high-precision time synchronization solution that ensures that devices in distributed systems maintain consistent time. Compared to previous technologies, PTP has the following advantages:
[P5089|Item List] Improved time synchronization accuracy: PTP achieves sub-microsecond time synchronization accuracy, which is significantly more precise than the sub-second accuracy of traditional NTP (Network Time Protocol). This high precision better meets the needs of many real-time applications.
[P5090|Item List] Applicability to various network topologies: PTP is applicable to any network topology, whether star, tree, or mesh, enabling high-precision synchronization. This wide applicability makes PTP suitable for a range of applications.
[P5091|Item List] Hardware-assisted processing: PTP utilizes hardware assistance to achieve faster time synchronization. This hardware assistance significantly improves synchronization speed, reduces latency, and enhances real-time system performance.
[P5092|Item List] Scalability: The design of PTP is scalable, facilitating the integration of more devices and sensors. This scalability enables PTP to be used in a wide range of applications such as the Internet of Things and smart homes.
[P5093|Item List] Independence from specific transmission media: PTP is independent of specific transmission media and can achieve high-precision time synchronization on Ethernet, fiber optic cables, and other transmission media. This flexibility makes PTP more practical for a variety of applications.
[P5094|Normal] In summary, as a high-precision time synchronization protocol, PTP offers improved accuracy, broader applicability, faster processing, scalability, and flexibility compared to previous technologies. These advantages have made PTP an essential time synchronization technology in various fields.
[P5095|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5096|Heading 6] Abbreviation and Terminology
[P5097|Table Description] Abbreviation 

[TABLE 15] rows=6 cols=2
R1	Abbreviation	Description
R2	GPS	Global Positioning System
R3	NTP	Network Time Protocol
R4	PTP	Precision Time Protocol
R5	UTC	Coordinated Universal Time
R6	TAI	International Atomic Time

[P5098|Heading 6] Basic principle
[P5099|Normal] The following are some important concepts in PTP, which can help users understand the function of PTP and configure it based on these understandings.
[P5100|Body Text] PTP Domain
[P5101|Body Text] The concept of PTP domain refers to the network that applies the Precision Time Protocol, also known as the PTP domain. In a PTP domain, there is only one master clock, and all devices are synchronized with this clock. Devices in the PTP domain can exchange time information through the PTP protocol, and perform time calibration and synchronization.
[P5102|Body Text] The supported range of PTP domain is 0-255. The PTP domain can be configured by command. The default domain is 0.
[P5103|Body Text] Clock
[P5104|Body Text] There are three clock types in the PTP protocol:
[P5105|Item List] Boundary Clock(BC): In the same PTP domain，the device with two or more ports participating in PTP time synchronization are called Boundary Clocks. The device synchronize time fron upstream devices through one port and distribute time to downstream devices through other ports. If the source clock distributes time to downstream devices through two or more ports, it is also called Boundary Clock.
[P5106|Item List] Ordinary Clock(OC): In the same PTP domain，the device with only one port participating in PTP time synchronization are called Ordinary Clocks. An ordinary clock either acts as the master clock providing the clock source or serves as the ultimate terminal, acquiring the clock from other clock sources without being able to act as an intermediate node to propagate the clock to other nodes.
[P5107|Item List] Transparent Clock(TC): As an intermediate node, a transparent clock receives the PTP packet without termination. It has a residence time bridge to calculate the residence time of the packet at this node, which is used to correct the time label before it is passed on.
[P5108|Normal] Port
[P5109|Body Text] The ports with PTP protocol enabled are called PTP ports. There are two types in PTP ports:
[P5110|Item List] Master Port: The ports used to distribute time to downstream devices on BC or OC devices.
[P5111|Item List] Slave Port: The port used to receives time from upstream device on BC or OC devices.
[P5112|Item List] Passive Port：The ports does not receive or distribute time on BC devices.
[P5113|Normal] Grandmaster Clock
[P5114|Body Text] The Grandmaster Clock (GM) is the highest-level clock in the PTP domain and the reference time for the entire PTP domain. All clock nodes in the PTP domain are organized in a certain hierarchy, and the time of the optimal clock will eventually be synchronized to the entire PTP domain through the interaction of PTP protocol messages between clock nodes. Therefore, it is also known as the clock source. The optimal clock can be statically specified through manual configuration, or dynamically elected through the Best Master Clock (BMC) protocol.
[P5115|Body Text] BMC algorithm
[P5116|Body Text] In the BMC algorithm, the optimal clock is dynamically elected through the interaction of PTP protocol messages between clock nodes. Each clock node exchanges information such as the optimal clock priority, time level, and time accuracy carried in the Announce message, and finally selects a node as the optimal clock for the PTP domain.
[P5117|Body Text] BMC selects Master Clock according to the following fields:
[P5118|Item List] Priority1：The valid range is 0-255. The smaller number indicates higher priority. The default value is 128.
[P5119|Item List] Clock-Class: The valid range is 6/7/13/14/52/58/187/193/248. The smaller number indicates higher priority. . The default value is 248.
[P5120|Item List] Clock-Accuracy: The valid range is 0x20-0x31/0xFE. The smaller number indicates higher priority. . The default value is 0xFE.
[P5121|Item List] Priority2: The valid range is 0-255. The smaller number indicates higher priority. The default value is 128.
[P5122|Normal] The priority sequence is Priority1＞Clock-Class＞Clock-Accuracy＞Priority2. If Priority1 of two devices are same, it should compare the Clock-Class, and so on. The device with higher Priority/class/accuracy becomes the master clock.
[P5123|Heading 6] Packet encapsulation
[P5124|Normal] The synchronization process of PTP is based on PTP packets interaction. The downstream device calculates the offset and delay from the master according to the timestamp in the packets, and adjusts the local clock to synchronize with the master clock.
[P5125|Body Text] The PTP timestamp is added by ASIC to ensure the precision of PTP time. The ASIC chip has higher performance than the software.
[P5126|Body Text] PTP packets support MAC encapsulation and UDP(IPv4/IPv6) encapsulation.
[P5127|Normal] 
[P5128|Figure Description] PTP packets
[P5129|Heading 6] Synchronization process
[P5130|Normal] The PTP time synchronization process involves the following steps:
[P5131|Item List] Selecting master and slave clocks: In the PTP synchronization process, one node is selected as the Master clock, and the other nodes serve as Slave clocks. The Master clock has a high-precision clock source and sends time information to the Slave clocks through the network, while the Slave clocks synchronize their clocks by correcting themselves.
[P5132|Item List] Clock identification and initialization: Nodes first need to identify each clock and initialize relevant parameters for the Master clock and Slave clocks, including clock frequency, delay, etc.
[P5133|Item List] Message passing between clocks: The core mechanism of PTP synchronization is to achieve time synchronization through message passing on the network. The Master clock periodically sends Sync messages to the network, and the Slave clocks receive the Sync messages and return corresponding Follow Up messages.
[P5134|Item List] Delay compensation and correction: During the PTP synchronization process, delay compensation is required due to message transmission delays. By calculating the transmission time of messages, delays can be compensated to ensure time accuracy. Simultaneously, based on the time difference between the Master clock and Slave clocks, the Slave clock corrects its clock.
[P5135|Item List] Fault tolerance mechanisms and optimization: In practical networks, due to factors such as complex network topologies and unstable link qualities, PTP synchronization may fail or lose precision. Therefore, during the PTP synchronization process, considerations for fault tolerance mechanisms are essential to improve system stability. Additionally, network conditions can be optimized for PTP synchronization, such as selecting better Master clocks or adjusting synchronization periods.
[P5136|Item List] Verification of time consistency: The verification of time consistency is also essential in the PTP synchronization process. Common verification methods include monitoring the time difference between Master clocks and Slave clocks, as well as assessing synchronization accuracy.
[P5137|Normal] This process can be described in detail through the delay request-response mechanism in the IEEE 1588 standard. The Master clock periodically sends Sync messages and records the precise time t1 when the message leaves; the Slave clock records the precise time t2 when the Sync message arrives; the Master clock sends a Follow_up message containing t1; the Slave clock sends a Delay_Req message, records the precise time t3 when the message leaves; the Master clock records the precise time t4 when the Delay_Req message arrives; subsequently, the Master clock sends a Delay_Resp message containing t4 to the Slave clock. Through this method, Master and Slave clocks can achieve time synchronization.

[P5144|Figure Description] PTP Timing Domain
[P5145|Body Text] As shown in the Figure above，Switch1 is the master in the domain, it distributes time to downstream devices. Switch2 receives time from Switch1 and send to Switch3. Switch3 receives time only.
[P5146|Heading 5] Configuration Steps
[P5147|Heading 6] Configuration of Switch1
[P5148|Step] Enter the configuration mode
[P5149|Terminal Display] Switch1# configure terminal
[P5150|Step] Enable PTP globally and set priority1
[P5151|Body Text] Switch1 is an ordinary clock with only one interface to distribute the time.
[P5152|Body Text] Configure priority1 as 0. This will lead the Switch have the highest priority in this PTP timing domain, that means, it is the master clock of this domain.
[P5153|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# ptp priority1 0
[P5154|Step] Configure clock-step(Optional)
[P5155|Body Text] Time-stamp in PTP packec support one-step and two-step mode. The default configration is two-step.
[P5156|Item List] one-step: It add the time-stamp into the Sync packet.
[P5157|Item List] two-step：It add the time-stamp of the Sync packet into the Follow_Up packet.
[P5158|Normal] It is suggested to use same clock-step in one PTP domain.
[P5159|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# ptp clock-step two-step
[P5160|Step] Configure the delay mechanism mode(Optional)
[P5161|Body Text] There are two mechanism modes: E2E/P2P.
[P5162|Item List] e2e: use the req-resp delay measurement mechanism.
[P5163|Item List] p2p: use a node delay measurement mechanism
[P5164|Normal] The default configuration is “e2e” mode.
[P5165|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# ptp delay-mechanism p2p
[P5166|Step] Enable PTP on the interface
[P5167|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch1(config-if)# ptp enable
[P5168|Step] Global Enable PTP
[P5169|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# ptp start
[P5170|Heading 6] Configuration of Switch2
[P5171|Step] Enter the configuration mode
[P5172|Terminal Display] Switch2# configure terminal
[P5173|Step] Set device type as boundary clock and Enable PTP globally

[P5176|Step] Configure the delay mechanism mode(Optional)
[P5177|Body Text] Note： Please use same configuration as Switch1.
[P5178|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# ptp delay-mechanism p2p
[P5179|Step] Enable PTP on the interface

Switch2(config-if)# ptp enable
Switch2(config-if)# exit

Switch2(config-if)# ptp enable
Switch2(config-if)# exit

[P5270|Heading 2] Configuring Phy Loopback
[P5271|Heading 3] Overview
[P5272|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5273|Normal] Phy loopback is a proprietary based loopback. There are 2 types of phy loopback: phy(including internal and external) level loopback and port level loopback.
[P5274|Item List] If a physical port is configured as “external phy loopback”, all packets coming into this port should be loopback back from the port itself at phy level.
[P5275|Item List] If a physical port is configured as “internal phy loopback”, all packets expected out from this port should be looped back to specified physical port.
[P5276|Item List] If a physical port is configured as “port loopback”, all packets coming into this port should be looped back from the port itself, and whether to swap the SMAC with the DMAC should be selectable by users. And if the MAC is swapped, the CRC should be recalculated.
[P5277|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5278|Normal] N/A
[P5279|Heading 3] Configuration
[P5280|Heading 4] Configuring external phy loopback

[P5315|Heading 2] Configuring L2 ping
[P5316|Heading 3] Overview
[P5317|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5318|Normal] The tool L2 ping is a useful application which’s purpose is detecting the connection between two switches. The L2 ping tool is not same with the well-known ‘ping IP-ADDRESS’ in the WINDOWS system. The normal “ping” is realized by the protocol ICMP which is dependent on the IP layer, so it may be inapplicable if the destination device is only Layer 2 switch. But the protocol used by L2 ping is only relying on Layer 2 ethernet packets.
[P5319|Body Text] When L2 ping is started, the L2 ping protocol packet (with ether type ‘36873(0x9009)’) is sent from a specified physical port to another specified destination port. At the destination end, the L2 ping protocol will be sent back via non 802.1ag loopback, or via a configuration “l2 ping response”. The device which is pinging, will receive the ping response packet, and print the ping result.
[P5320|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5321|Normal] N/A
[P5322|Heading 3] Configuration
[P5323|Normal] 
[P5324|Figure Description] ping a switch port
[P5325|Body Text] The configurations are almost same on Switch1 and Switch2, except the parts which are specially pointed out.
[P5326|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P5327|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P5328|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the interface configure mode and turn up the interface
[P5329|Terminal Display] Switch (config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch (config-if)# no shutdown
[P5330|Heading 5] step 3 Enable the L2 ping response function
[P5331|Normal] Configure on Switch2:
[P5332|Terminal Display] Switch (config-if)# l2 ping response enable
[P5333|Heading 5] step 4 Exit the configure mode
[P5334|Terminal Display] Switch (config-if)# end
[P5335|Heading 5] step 5 Using L2 ping
[P5336|Normal] Operate on Switch1:
[P5337|Terminal Display] Switch1# l2 ping 001e.0808.58f1 interface eth-0-1 count 10 interval 1000 timeout 2000

 64 bytes from 001e.0808.58f1: sequence = 6, time = 12ms

[P5339|Heading 2] Configuring RMON
[P5340|Heading 3] Overview
[P5341|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5342|Normal] RMON is an Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) standard monitoring specification that allows various network agents and console systems to exchange network monitoring data. You can use the RMON feature with the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) agent in the switch to monitor all the traffic flowing among switched on all connected LAN segments.
[P5343|Body Text] RMON is a standard monitoring specification that defines a set of statistics and functions that can be exchanged between RMON-compliant console systems and network probes RMON provides you with comprehensive network-fault diagnosis, planning, and performance-tuning information.
[P5344|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5345|Normal] N/A
[P5346|Heading 3] Configuration
[P5347|Normal] 
[P5348|Figure Description] rmon
[P5349|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P5350|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P5351|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the interface configure mode and create a stats and a history
[P5352|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# rmon collection stats 1 owner test
Switch(config-if)# rmon collection history 1 buckets 100 interval 1000 owner test
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P5353|Heading 5] step 3 Create an event with log and trap both set.
[P5354|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# rmon event 1 log trap public description test_event owner test
[P5355|Heading 5] step 4 Create a alarm using event 1 we created before and monitor the alarm on ETHERSTATSBROADCASTPKTS on eth-0-1
[P5356|Terminal Display]  Switch(config)# rmon alarm 1 etherStatsEntry.6.1 interval 1000 delta rising-threshold 1000 event 1 falling-threshold 1 event 1 owner test  
[P5357|Heading 5] step 5 Exit the configure mode
[P5358|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end

[P5361|Heading 2] Configuring SNMP
[P5362|Heading 3] Overview
[P5363|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5364|Normal] SNMP is an application-layer protocol that provides a message format for communication between managers and agents. The SNMP system consists of an SNMP manager, an SNMP agent, and a MIB. The SNMP manager can be part of a network management system (NMS). The agent and MIB reside on the switch. To configure SNMP on the switch, you define the relationship between the manager and the agent. The SNMP agent contains MIB variables whose values the SNMP manager can request or change. A manager can get a value from an agent or store a value into the agent. The agent gathers data from the MIB, the repository for information about device parameters and network data. The agent can also respond to a manager’s requests to get or set data. An agent can send unsolicited traps to the manager. Traps are messages alerting the SNMP manager to a condition on the network. Error user authentication, restarts, link status (up or down), MAC address tracking, closing of a Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connection, loss of connection to a neighbor, or other significant events may send a trap.
[P5365|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5366|Normal] SNMP module is based on the following RFC draft:
[P5367|Item List] SNMPv1: Defined in RFC 1157.
[P5368|Item List] SNMPv2C: Defined in RFC 1901.
[P5369|Item List] SNMPv3: Defined in RFC 2273 to 2275.
[P5370|Normal] Following is a brief description of terms and concepts used to describe the SNMP protocol:
[P5371|Item List] Agent: A network-management software module, an agent has local knowledge of management information and translates that information into a form compatible with SNMP.
[P5372|Item List] Management Information Base (MIB): Management Information Base, collection of information is organized hierarchically.
[P5373|Item List] Engine ID: A unique ID for a network’s node.
[P5374|Item List] Trap: Used by managed devices to asynchronously report events to the NMS.
[P5375|Heading 3] Configuration
[P5376|Normal] 
[P5377|Figure Description] snmp
[P5378|Body Text] As shown in the figure SNMP agent gathers data from the MIB. The agent can send traps, or notification of certain events, to the SNMP manager, which receives and processes the traps. Traps alert the SNMP manager to a condition on the network such as improper user authentication, restarts, link status (up or down), MAC address tracking, and so forth. The SNMP agent also responds to MIB-related queries sent by the SNMP manager in get-request, get-next-request, and set-request format.
[P5379|Heading 4] Enable SNMP
[P5380|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P5381|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P5382|Heading 5] step 2 Enable SNMP globally
[P5383|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# snmp-server enable
[P5384|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P5385|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P5386|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P5387|Terminal Display] Switch# show running-config
snmp-server enable
[P5388|Heading 4] Configuring community string
[P5389|Normal] You use the SNMP community string to define the relationship between the SNMP manager and the agent. The community string acts like a password to permit access to the agent on the switch. Optionally, you can specify one or more of these characteristics associated with the string:
[P5390|Item List] A MIB view, which defines the subset of all MIB objects accessible to the given community
[P5391|Item List] Read and write or read-only permission for the MIB objects accessible to the community
[P5392|Normal] Beginning in privileged EXEC mode, follow these steps to configure a community string on the switch.
[P5393|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P5394|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P5395|Heading 5] step 2 Configuring community string
[P5396|Normal] Configure a view named “DUT”(optional); Configure a community named “public” with read access and view “DUT”.
[P5397|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# snmp-server view DUT included 1
Switch(config)# snmp-server community public read-write (view DUT)
[P5398|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P5399|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P5400|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P5401|Terminal Display] Switch# show running-config
snmp-server enable
snmp-server view DUT included .1 
snmp-server community public read-only view DUT
[P5402|Heading 4] Configuring SNMPv3 Groups, Users and Accesses
[P5403|Normal] You can specify an identification name (engine ID) for the local SNMP server engine on the switch. You can configure an SNMP server group that maps SNMP users to SNMP views, you can add new users to the SNMP group, and you can add access for the SNMP group.
[P5404|Body Text] Beginning in privileged EXEC mode, follow these steps to configure SNMP on the switch.
[P5405|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P5406|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P5407|Heading 5] step 2 Set the globle configurations for SNMP
[P5408|Normal] Set engineID; Set the user name, password, and authentication type; Create SNMP server; Set the authority for the group member.
[P5409|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# snmp-server engineID 8000123456
Switch(config)# snmp-server usm-user usr1 authentication md5 mypassword privacy des yourpassword
Switch(config)# snmp-server group grp1 user usr1 security-model usm
Switch(config)# snmp-server access grp1 security-model usm noauth
[P5410|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P5411|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P5412|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P5413|Terminal Display] Switch# show running-config
snmp-server engineID 8000123456 
snmp-server usm-user usr1 authentication md5 mypassword privacy des yourpassword 
snmp-server group grp1 user usr1 security-model usm 
snmp-server access grp1 security-model usm noauth

[P5415|Normal] Beginning in privileged EXEC mode, follow these steps to configure SNMP on the switch.

[P5435|Heading 2] Configuring SFLOW
[P5436|Heading 3] Overview
[P5437|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5438|Normal] sFlow is a technology for monitoring traffic in data networks containing switches and routers. In particular, it defines the sampling mechanisms implemented in a sFlow Agent for monitoring traffic, and the format of sample data used by the sFlow Agent when forwarding data to a central data collector.
[P5439|Body Text] The architecture and sampling techniques used in the sFlow monitoring system are designed to provide continuous site-wide (and network-wide) traffic monitoring for high speed switched and routed networks.
[P5440|Body Text] The sFlow Agent uses two forms of sampling: statistical packet-based sampling of switched flows, and time-based sampling of network interface statistics.
[P5441|Body Text] Default Configuration for sflow：

[TABLE 17] rows=5 cols=2
R1	Feature	Default Setting
R2	global sflow	disabled
R3	sflow on port	disable
R4	collector udp port	6343
R5	counter interval time	20 seconds

[P5442|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5443|Normal] N/A
[P5444|Heading 3] Configuration
[P5445|Normal] 
[P5446|Figure Description] sflow
[P5447|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P5448|Terminal Display]  Switch# configure terminal
[P5449|Heading 5] step 2 Enable sflow globally
[P5450|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# sflow enable
[P5451|Heading 5] step 3 Set the global attribute for sflow
[P5452|Normal] Set the agent IP address，set the collector IP address and udp port. If the udp port is not specified, it means default port 6364.
[P5453|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# sflow agent ip 3.3.3.1
Switch(config)# sflow collector 3.3.3.2 6342
[P5454|Normal] Set the agent and collector with IPv6:
[P5455|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# sflow agent ipv6 2001:2000::2 
Switch(config)# sflow collector 2001:2000::1
[P5456|Normal] At list one Agent and one collector must be configured for sflow. User can use IPv4 or IPv6.
[P5457|Body Text] Set the interval to send interface counter information (optional):
[P5458|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# sflow counter interval 15
[P5459|Heading 5] step 4 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interfaces
[P5460|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# ip address 15.1.1.1/24
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)#no switchport
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# ip address 16.1.1.1/24
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-3
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# ip address 3.3.3.1/24
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P5461|Heading 5] step 5 Enable sflow for input packets on eth-0-1

Switch(config-if)# sflow flow-sampling rate 8192
Switch(config-if)# sflow flow-sampling enable input
Switch(config-if)# sflow counter-sampling enable

[P5468|Heading 2] Configuring LLDP
[P5469|Heading 3] Overview
[P5470|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5471|Normal] LLDP（Link Layer Discovery Protocol）is the discovery protocol on link layer defined as standard in IEEE 802.1ab. Discovery on Layer 2 can locate interfaces attached to the devices exactly with connection information on layer 2, such as VLAN attribute of port and protocols supported, and present paths among client, switch, router, application servers and other network servers. This detailed description is helpful to get useful information for diagnosing network fast, like topology of devices attached, conflict configuration between devices, and reason of network failure.
[P5472|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5473|Normal] N/A
[P5474|Heading 3] Configuration
[P5475|Normal] 
[P5476|Figure Description] lldp
[P5477|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P5478|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P5479|Heading 5] step 2 Enable SNMP globally
[P5480|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# lldp enable
[P5481|Heading 5] step 3 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of LLDP on the interface
[P5482|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch(config)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# no lldp tlv 8021-org-specific vlan-name
Switch(config-if)# lldp tlv med location-id ecs-elin 1234567890
Switch(config-if)# lldp enable txrx
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P5483|Heading 5] step 4 Set LLDP timers (optional)
[P5484|Normal] Configure the transmitting interval of LLDP packet to 40 seconds; Configure the transmitting delay of LLDP packet to 3 seconds; Configure the reinit delay of LLDP function to 1 second.
[P5485|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# lldp timer msg-tx-interval 40
Switch(config)# lldp timer tx-delay 3
Switch(config)# lldp timer reinitDelay 1
[P5486|Heading 5] step 5 Exit the configure mode
[P5487|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end

[P5491|Heading 2] Configuring IPFIX
[P5492|Heading 3] Overview
[P5493|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P5494|Normal] Traffic on a data network can be seen as consisting of flows passing through network elements. For administrative or other purposes, it is often interesting, useful, or even necessary to have access to information about these flows that pass through the network elements. This requires uniformity in the method of representing the flow information and the means of communicating the flows from the network elements to the collection point. This is what IPFIX can do.
[P5495|Body Text] Before IPFIX was introduced, there is a Cisco private method NetFlow. IPFIX is similar to NetFlow and is based on NetFlow version 9.
[P5496|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5497|Normal] N/A
[P5498|Heading 3] Configuration
[P5499|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P5500|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P5501|Heading 5] step 2 Set the aging time(optional)
[P5502|Normal] Set the aging time as 300 seconds. The aging time is 1800 seconds by default.
[P5503|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ipfix global
Switch(Config-ipfix-global)# flow aging 300
[P5504|Heading 5] step 3 Configuring recorder
[P5505|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ipfix recorder recorder1
Switch(Config-ipfix-reocrder)# match mac source address
Switch(Config-ipfix-reocrder)# match ipv4 source address mask 32
Switch(Config-ipfix-reocrder)# match ipv4 destination address mask 32
Switch(Config-ipfix-reocrder)# match vxlan-vni

[P5521|Heading 2] ConfiguringHardware Monitor
[P5522|Heading 3] Overview
[P5523|Heading 4] Brief Introduction
[P5524|Normal] The Hardware Monitor monitors network traffic at the Hardware level. It monitors network congestion in real time and reports the traffic to the network administrator for corresponding traffic management policies. The Hardware Monitor includes two modules: Buffer Monitor and Latency Monitor.
[P5525|Item List] Buffer Monitor: Buffer Monitor monitors the usage of the buffer cell of a port and reports congestion events in real time.
[P5526|Item List] Latency Monitor: Latency Monitor monitors the latency of packets, reports latency events in real time, and discards packets with high latency.
[P5527|Normal] In addition, the Hardware Monitor provides watermark and notification functions.
[P5528|Item List] Watermark Function: The watermark function records the maximum buffer cell usage and packet forwarding delay of a port within a period of time.
[P5529|Item List] Notification Function: The notification function sends data collected by the Hardware Monitor module and reported events to the specified notification server.
[P5530|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P5531|Normal] The Hardware Monitor is divided into Buffer Monitor module and Latency Monitor module. The principles of these modules are described as follows.
[P5532|Heading 5] Principle Description Of Buffer Monitor
[P5533|Normal] The schematic diagram of the Buffer Monitor module is as follows:
[P5534|Normal] 
[P5535|Figure Description] Buffer Monitor Principle description
[P5536|Body Text] When the traffic forwarded to an interface of the switch exceeds its maximum forwarding capability, the switch caches the packets that cannot be forwarded immediately and forwards them when congestion is relieved or relieved. The minimum unit used by the chip of Shengke switch to cache packets is the buffer cell. Network congestion can be determined by monitoring the occupation of the buffer cell of the port.
[P5537|Body Text] On an interface with the Buffer Monitor function enabled, the switch samples the usage of the interface’s buffer cell every 10ms and stamps the time. When the number of buffer cells occupied by an interface exceeds the High Threshold, the switch immediately reports a congestion start event to the CPU with the time stamp of the event. When the number of buffer cells occupied by an interface decreases form the High Threshold to the Low Threshold, the switch immediately reports a congestion end event to the CPU with the time stamp of the event. If the notification function of the Buffer Monitor module is enabled, the system sends a Buffer Stats Notify message to the notification server at an interval defined by the administrator. The message contains the name of the monitored port, the usage of the buffer cell, and the timestamp when data is reported. When a congestion event occurs or ends, the system immediately sends a Micro-burst Start Notify and Micro-burst Stop Notify packet to the notification server. The content is also the name of the monitored port, buffer cell usage, and time stamp of the event report.
[P5538|Heading 5] Principle Description Of Latency Monitor
[P5539|Normal] The Latency Monitor module works as follows:
[P5540|Normal] 
[P5541|Figure Description] Latency Monitor Principle description
[P5542|Body Text] The Latency Monitor module calculates the latency of packets forwarded within the switch. You can configure eight latency intervals. On interfaces with Latency Monitor enabled, the switch calculates the number of packets in each latency interval every 10ms.
[P5543|Body Text] When the packet forwarding delay exceeds the High Threshold, the switch immediately reports a delay start event to the CPU, along with the timestamp when the event occurs, the packet forwarding delay, and the packet inbound port information. When the packet forwarding delay is lower than the Low Threshold, the switch immediately reports a delay end event to the CPU with the event occurrence time stamp, packet forwarding delay, and packet inbound port information. If the forwarding delay of a packet on a port with high forwarding delay is greater than Drop Threshold, the packet will be discarded. If the Latency Monitor notification function is enabled, the system sends Latency Stats Notify packets to the notification server at an interval defined by the administartor. The Latency Stats Notify packets contain the name of the monitored port and the number of packets in each interval. When a latency event starts or ends, the system sends a Latency Event Start Notify and Latency Event Stop Notify packet to the notification server. These packets contain the name of the monitoring port and the inbound port name of the packet that triggers the event, the forwarding delay of the packet triggering the event and the timestamp when the event occurred.
[P5544|Heading 4] ·Configure Buffer Monitor
[P5545|Normal] The following example shows how to enable the buffer monitor function on port eth-0-9 and the congestion event reporting function of the system. Set the high and low thresholds for reporting congestion events to 32000 and 64 buffer cells.
[P5546|Step] Enter the configure mode

[P5548|Step] Enter the interface configure mode

[P5567|Heading 4] Configure Latency Monitor
[P5568|Normal] The following example show how to enable the Latency Monitor and high-latency packet discard function on port eth-0-9, configure eight latency ranges, and set the latency event trigger threshold and high-latency packet discard threshold.
