[P7887|Heading 2] Configuring VRRP
[P7888|Heading 3] Overview
[P7889|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P7890|Normal] This chapter provides an overview of Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) and its implementation. VRRP eliminates the risk of a single point of failure inherent in a static default routing environment. It specifies an election protocol that dynamically assigns responsibility for a virtual router to one of the VRRP routers on a LAN. One of the major advantages of VRRP is that it makes default path available without requiring configuration of dynamic routing on every end-host.
[P7891|Body Text]  MD5 authentication is not yet supported for VRRP.
[P7892|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P7893|Normal] The VRRP module is based on: RFC 3768 (VRRP): Knight, S., et.al “Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP)”
[P7894|Body Text] Terminology
[P7895|Item List] Backup Router： VRRP router that back up an IP address. It assumes forwarding responsibility for the virtual IP address if the Master fails.
[P7896|Item List] Critical IP： The IP address that the VRRP router send/receive messages on for a particular session.
[P7897|Item List] IP Address Owner： The VRRP Router that has the virtual router’s IP address (es) as real interface address (es). This is the router that, when up, will respond to packets addressed to one of these IP addresses for ICMP pings, TCP connections, etc.
[P7898|Item List] Master Router： The VRRP router that owns the IP address (i.e., is being backed up), and which is the default router for forwarding for that IP address.
[P7899|Item List] Virtual IP： The IP address back up by a VRRP session.
[P7900|Item List] Virtual Router： A router managed by VRRP that acts as a default router for hosts on a shared LAN. It consists of a Virtual Router Identifier and a set of associated IP addresses across a common LAN. A VRRP Router might backup one or more virtual routers.
[P7901|Item List] VRRP Router： A router runs the Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol. It might participate in one or more virtual routers.
[P7902|Normal] Typically, end hosts are connected to the enterprise network through a single router (first hop router) that is in the same Local Area Network (LAN) segment. The most popular method of configuration for the end hosts is to statically configure this router as their default gateway. This minimizes configuration and processing overhead. The main problem with this configuration method is that it produces a single point of failure if this first hop router fails.
[P7903|Normal] 
[P7904|Figure Description] Without VRRP
[P7905|Body Text] The Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol attempts to solve this problem by introducing the concept of a virtual router, composed of two or more VRRP routers on the same subnet. The concept of a virtual IP address is also introduced, which is the address that end hosts configure as their default gateway. Only one router (called the master) forward packets on the behalf of this IP address. In the event that the Master router fails, one of the other routers (Backup) assumes forwarding responsibility for it.
[P7906|Normal] 
[P7907|Figure Description] With VRRP
[P7908|Body Text] At first glance, the configuration outlined in might not seem very useful, as it doubles the cost and leaves one router idle at all times. This, however, can be avoided by creating two virtual routers and splitting the traffic between them.
[P7909|Heading 3] Configuration
[P7910|Heading 4] Configuring VRRP (One Virtual Router)
[P7911|Normal] 
[P7912|Figure Description] VRRP with one virtual router
[P7913|Body Text] In this configuration the end-hosts install a default route to the IP address of virtual router 1(VRID = 1) and both routers R1 and R2 run VRRP. R1 is configured to be the Master for virtual router 1 (VRID = 1) and R2 as a Backup for virtual router 1. If R1 fails, R2 will take over virtual router 1 and its IP addresses, and provide uninterrupted service for the hosts. Configuring only one virtual router, doubles the cost and leaves R2 idle at all times.
[P7914|Body Text] The following configuration should be operated on all devices if the device ID is not specified.

[P7916|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P7917|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface

Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

[P7961|Heading 4] VRRP Circuit Failover
[P7962|Normal] 
[P7963|Figure Description] VRRP Circuit Failover
[P7964|Body Text] The need for VRRP Circuit Failover arose because VRRPv2 was unable to track the gateway interface status. The VRRP Circuit Failover feature provides a dynamic failover of an entire circuit in the event that one member of the group fails. It introduces the concept of a circuit, where two or more Virtual Routers on a single system can be grouped. In the event that a failure occurs and one of the Virtual Routers performs the Master to Backup transition, the other Virtual Routers in the group are notified and are forced into the Master to Backup transition, so that both incoming and outgoing packets are routed through the same gateway router, eliminating the problem for Firewall/NAT environments. The following scenario explains this feature.
[P7965|Body Text] To configure VRRP Circuit Failover, each circuit is configured to have a corresponding priority-delta value, which is passed to VRRP when a failure occurs. The priority of each Virtual Router on the circuit is decremented by the priority delta value causing the VR Master to VR Backup transition.
[P7966|Body Text] In this example, two routers R1 and R2 are configured as backup routers with different priorities. The priority-delta value is configured to be greater than the difference of both the priorities. R1 is configured to have a priority of 100 and R2 has a priority of 90. R1 with a greater priority is the Virtual Router Master. The priority-delta value is 20, greater than 10 (100 minus 90). On R1 when the external interface eth1 fails, the priority of R1 becomes 80 (100 minus 20). Since R2 has a greater priority (90) than R1, R2 becomes the VR Master and routing of packages continues without interruption.
[P7967|Body Text] When this VR Backup (R1) is up again, it regains its original priority (100) and becomes the VR Master again.
[P7968|Body Text] The following configuration should be operated on all devices if the device ID is not specified.
[P7969|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P7970|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P7971|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface
[P7972|Normal] Interface configuration for R1:
[P7973|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.10.10.50/24
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.10.11.50/24
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P7974|Normal] Interface configuration for R2:
[P7975|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.10.10.40/24
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P7976|Heading 5] step 3 Create an track object to monitor the link state
[P7977|Normal] Configuring R1:
[P7978|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# track 10 interface eth-0-2 linkstate
[P7979|Normal] To get more information about track, please reference to the “Configuring Track” chapter.
[P7980|Heading 5] step 4 Create an instance of vrrp
[P7981|Normal] Configuring R1:
[P7982|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# router vrrp 1
Switch(config-router)# virtual-ip 10.10.10.1
Switch(config-router)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-router)# preempt-mode true 
Switch(config-router)# advertisement-interval 5
Switch(config-router)# priority 100
Switch(config-router)# track 10 decrement 20
Switch(config-router)# enable
[P7983|Normal] Configuring R2:
[P7984|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# router vrrp 1
Switch(config-router)# virtual-ip 10.10.10.1
Switch(config-router)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-router)# preempt-mode true 
Switch(config-router)# advertisement-interval 5
Switch(config-router)# priority 90
Switch(config-router)# enable
[P7985|Heading 5] step 5 Exit the configure mode
[P7986|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end

[P7995|Body Text] In this configuration the end-hosts install a default route to the IP address of virtual router 1(VRID = 1) and both routers R1 and R2 run VRRP. R1 is configured to be the Master for virtual router 1 (VRID = 1) and R2 as a Backup for virtual router 1. If R1 fails, R2 will take over virtual router 1 and its IP addresses, and provide uninterrupted service for the hosts. Configuring only one virtual router, doubles the cost and leaves R2 idle at all times.

Switch(config-if)# no shutdown

[P8047|Body Text] To configure VRRP Circuit Failover, each circuit is configured to have a corresponding priority-delta value, which is passed to VRRP when a failure occurs. [P8081|Heading 3] Application cases

[P8083|Heading 2] Configuring Track
[P8084|Heading 3] Overview
[P8085|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P8086|Normal] Track is used for link the functional modules and monitor modules. Track builds a system structure with 3 levels: “functional modules – Track – monitor modules”.
[P8087|Body Text] Track can shield the difference of the monitor modules and provide an unitized API for the functional modules.
[P8088|Body Text] The following monitor modules are supported:
[P8089|Item List] IP SLA
[P8090|Item List] interface states
[P8091|Item List] bfd states
[P8092|Normal] The following functional modules are supported:
[P8093|Item List] Static route
[P8094|Item List] VRRP
[P8095|Normal] Track makes a communication for the functional modules and monitor modules. When link states or network performance is changed, the monitor modules can detect the event and notify the track module; therefore track will change its owner states and notify the related functional modules.
[P8096|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P8097|Normal] N/A
[P8098|Heading 3] Configuration
[P8099|Heading 4] Configuring IP SLA for interfaces in the VRF
[P8100|Normal] 
[P8101|Figure Description] IP SLA
[P8102|Body Text] IP SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a network performance measurement and diagnostics tool that uses active monitoring. Active monitoring is the generation of traffic in a reliable and predictable manner to measure network performance. Every IP SLA operation maintains an operation return-code value. This return code is interpreted by the tracking process. The return code can return OK, Over Threshold, and several other return codes. Different operations can have different return-code values, so only values common to all operation types are used. In IP SLA, use icmp echo to check state or reachability of a route.
[P8103|Body Text] The following configuration should be operated on all switches if the switch ID is not specified.
[P8104|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P8105|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P8106|Heading 5] step 2 Create a vrf instance
[P8107|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ip vrf vpn1
Switch(config-vrf)# exit
[P8108|Heading 5] step 3 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface
[P8109|Normal] Interface configuration for Switch1:
[P8110|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# ip vrf forwarding vpn1
Switch(config-if)# ip address 192.168.0.2/24
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P8111|Normal] Interface configuration for Switch2:
[P8112|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# ip vrf forwarding vpn1
Switch(config-if)# ip address 192.168.0.1/24
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P8113|Heading 5] step 4 Create ip sla and set the attributes
[P8114|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8115|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ip sla monitor 1
Switch(config-ipsla)# type icmp-echo 192.168.0.1
Switch(config-ipsla)# frequency 35
Switch(config-ipsla)# timeout 6
Switch(config-ipsla)# threshold 3000
Switch(config-ipsla)# ttl 65
Switch(config-ipsla)# tos 1
Switch(config-ipsla)# data-size 29
Switch(config-ipsla)# data-pattern abababab
Switch(config-ipsla)# fail-percent 90
Switch(config-ipsla)# packets-per-test 4
Switch(config-ipsla)# interval 9
Switch(config-ipsla)# statistics packet 10
Switch(config-ipsla)# statistics test 3
Switch(config-ipsla)# vrf vpn1
Switch(config-ipsla)# exit
[P8116|Normal]  Parameters for ip sla:
[P8117|Item List] frequency:Time between 2 probes. Valid range is 1-4800 second, default value is 60 seconds.
[P8118|Item List] timeout:Timeout value for icmp reply. Valid range is 1-4800 second, default value is 5 seconds.
[P8119|Item List] threshold: Timeout value for icmp threshold. Valid range is 1-4800000 millisecond, default value is 5000 millisecond.
[P8120|Item List] packets-per-test:Packet number for each probe. Valid range is 1-10, default value is 3.
[P8121|Item List] interval:Time between 2 packets. Valid range is 1-4800 second, default value is 6 seconds.
[P8122|Item List] statistics packet:Packet number for statistics. Valid range is 0-1000, default value is 50.
[P8123|Item List] statistics test probe number for statistics. Valid range is 0-10, default value is 5
[P8124|Heading 5] step 5 Enable ip sla
[P8125|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8126|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ip sla monitor schedule 1
[P8127|Heading 5] step 6 Exit the configure mode
[P8128|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P8129|Heading 5] step 7 Validation

[P8184|Heading 4] Configuring track interface linkstate
[P8185|Normal] 
[P8186|Figure Description] Track interface
[P8187|Body Text] Before the introduction of track feature, the VRRP had a simple tracking mechanism that allowed you to track the interface link state only. If the link state of the interface went down, the VRRP priority of the router was reduced, allowing another VRRP router with a higher priority to become active. The Track feature separates the tracking mechanism from VRRP and creates a separate standalone tracking process that can be used by other processes in future. This feature allows tracking of other objects in addition to the interface link state. VRRP can now register its interest in tracking objects and then be notified when the tracked object changes state. TRACK is a separate standalone tracking process that can be used by other processes as well as VRRP. This feature allows tracking of other objects in addition to the interface link state.
[P8188|Body Text] Configuring Switch1:
[P8189|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P8190|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P8191|Heading 5] step 2 Create track and set the attributes
[P8192|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# track 1 interface eth-0-1 linkstate
Switch(config-track)# delay up 30
Switch(config-track)# delay down 30
Switch(config-track)# exit
[P8193|Normal] []Parameters for track:
[P8194|Item List] delay up: After the interface states is up, the track will wait for a cycle before restore the states. Valid range is 1-180 second. The default configuration is restore without delay.
[P8195|Item List] delay down: After the interface states is down, the track will wait for a cycle before change the states. Valid range is 1-180 second. The default configuration is change without delay.
[P8196|Normal]  If the track is using bfd or ip sla, the “delay up” and “delay down” is similar as using interface states.
[P8197|Heading 5] step 3 Exit the configure mode
[P8198|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P8199|Heading 5] step 4 Validation
[P8200|Terminal Display] Switch#show track
Track 2
    Type                    : Interface Link state
    Interface              : eth-0-1
    State                   : down
    Delay up               : 30 seconds
Delay down                 : 30 seconds

[P8319|Heading 2] Configuring IP BFD
[P8320|Heading 3] Overview
[P8321|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P8322|Normal] An increasingly important feature of networking equipment is the rapid detection of communication failures between adjacent systems, in order to more quickly establish alternative paths. Detection can come fairly quickly in certain circumstances when data link hardware comes into play (such as Synchronous Optical Network (SONET) alarms). However, there are media that do not provide this kind of signaling (such as Ethernet), and some media may not detect certain kinds of failures in the path, for example, failing interfaces or forwarding engine components.
[P8323|Body Text] Networks use relatively slow “Hello” mechanisms, usually in routing protocols, to detect failures when there is no hardware signaling to help out. The time to detect failures (“Detection Times”) available in the existing protocols is no better than a second, which is far too long for some applications and represents a great deal of lost data at gigabit rates. Furthermore, routing protocol Hellos are of no help when those routing protocols are not in use, and the semantics of detection are subtly different – they detect a failure in the path between the two routing protocol engines.
[P8324|Body Text] The goal of Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) is to provide low-overhead, short-duration detection of failures in the path between adjacent forwarding engines, including the interfaces, data link(s), and, to the extent possible, the forwarding engines themselves.
[P8325|Body Text] An additional goal is to provide a single mechanism that can be used for aliveness detection over any media, at any protocol layer, with a wide range of Detection Times and overhead, to avoid a proliferation of different methods.
[P8326|Body Text] If ethernet CFM mep is configured on an physical port and CFM LM is enabled, at the same time, IP BFD is configured on an vlan interface and the former physical port is a member of the vlan, IP BFD can’t work normally. If CFM LM is disabled, IP BFD can work normally.
[P8327|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P8328|Normal] Reference RFC 5880 Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD)

[P8394|Heading 2] Configuring VARP
[P8395|Heading 3] Overview
[P8396|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P8397|Normal] Virtual ARP (VARP) allows multiple switches to simultaneously route packets with the same destination MAC address. Each switch is configured with the same virtual MAC address for the the L3 interfaces configured with a virtual IP address. In MLAG configurations, VARP is preferred over VRRP because VARP working on active-active mode without traffic traverse peer link.
[P8398|Body Text] For ARP and GARP requests to virtual IP address, VARP will use the virtual MAC address to reply. The virtual MAC address is only used in the destination field of inbound packets and never used in the source field of outbound packets.Topology

[P8428|Heading 1] Network Virtualization Configuration Guide
[P8429|Heading 2] Configuring VXLAN
[P8430|Heading 3] Overview
[P8431|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P8432|Normal] Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN) is a networking technology that encapsulates MAC-based Layer 2 Ethernet frames within Layer 3 UDP packets to aggregate and tunnel multiple layer 2 networks across a Layer 3 infrastructure. VXLAN scales up to 16 million logical networks and supports layer 2 adjacency across IP networks. Multicast transmission architecture is used for broadcast/multicast/unknown packets.
[P8433|Heading 4] Background
[P8434|Normal] Nowadays, Server virtualization gets more and more recognitions and deployments since it reduces the cost of IT, improves the flexibilities of business deployment and reduces the cost of maintenance and other advantages. One server can virtual into multiple virtual machines; one virtual machine is equal to a host, the number of hosts has a big change on its amount.
[P8435|Body Text] When virtual machine runs, it needs to move to new server because the resources of server and other problems (such as CPU is too high, the storage is not enough and so on). To make sure that business is not interrupted during the migration, it needs to make sure that the IP address, MAC address and other parameters of virtual machine are not changing. This is asking the business network as a Layer 2 network, and requires that the network itself has multiple paths of redundancy and reliabilities.
[P8436|Body Text] The above requirements make traditional Layer 2 domain becomes larger and larger. The traditional network becomes powerless to cope with larger Layer 2 requirements, it mainly reflected in the following aspects:
[P8437|Item List] Under the environment of larger Layer 2 networks, packets forwarding by looking up MAC address table; the volume of switch’s MAC address table limits the number of virtual machines
[P8438|Item List] Network isolates abilities limitation, the most popular isolation techniques are VLAN or VPN (Virtual Private Network). It has the following limitation that large size of virtual networks deploy: since IEEE 802.1Q defines that VLAN Tag domain only has 12 bit, so it only show 4096 VLAN which cannot satisfy users group’s requirement in large Layer 2 network.
[P8439|Item List] VLAN/VPN in traditional Layer 2 network cannot satisfy the requirement of network dynamic adjustment. The network structure limits the range that virtual machines migrate.
[P8440|Normal] Direct at the above problems in large Layer 2 network, the raise of VXLAN (Virtual eXtensible Local Area Network) solves the problems well.
[P8441|Item List] Aim to virtual machines suffer from network size limitation, VXLAN encapsulates the data packages that virtual machines send into UDP, and uses IP and MAC address from physical network as external header to encapsulate, then express the parameters after encapsulating to network. Hence, it rapidly reduces the requirements of MAC addresses’ size that large Layer 2 network requires.
[P8442|Item List] Direct at the network isolates abilities limitation, VXLAN imports users id which is similar as VLAN ID, that is consisted of 24 bit; it supports up to 16 million users and is satisfied by large amount of user id
[P8443|Item List] Aim to the range of virtual machines migrate is limited by network structure, Using VXLAN to construct large Layer 2 network makes sure the IP and MAC address are keeping the same during virtual machines migrate.
[P8444|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P8445|Heading 5] Basic principle
[P8446|Heading 6] Abbreviation and Terminology

[TABLE 21] rows=2 cols=2
R1	Abbreviation/Terminology	Description
R2	VTEP(VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint)	VETP is the terminated point of VXLAN tunnel, is the device that is used for encapsulating and decapsulating VXLAN packets

[P8447|Heading 6] Basic principle
[P8448|Normal] VXLAN is a kind of technique of network virtualization. Figure 2-1 shows the packet format of VXLAN, VXLAN packet adds a VXLAN header and UDP/IP header to the packet, original packets which are sent by VM or physical server, and uses added MAC/IP to forward on network devices that it passes through, then it restores the decapsulated packets on tunnel endpoint and sends the original packet to VM or physical server.
[P8449|Heading 6] Packet encapsulation
[P8450|Normal] 
[P8451|Figure Description] The packet format of VXLAN
[P8452|Body Text] VXLAN header encapsulates:
[P8453|Item List] Flag: 8 bit, current protocol value is 00001000, the fifth bit indicates whether the VXLAN packet is valid or not
[P8454|Item List] VNID: VXLAN Network Identifier, VXLAN network id, 24 bit, is used for distinguish VXLAN sections.
[P8455|Item List] Reserved: 24 bit and 8 bit, current protocol regulates that should be 0 for all.
[P8456|Normal] UCP header encapsulates:
[P8457|Item List] destination port number is 4789, source port number is depends the calculation of Hash value according to header contexts of original packets
[P8458|Normal] External IP header:
[P8459|Item List] The source ip is the IP of VTEP where the transmit server or virtual machine belongs to packet; the destination IP is the IP of VTEP server or virtual machine belongs to.
[P8460|Normal] External Ethernet header:
[P8461|Item List] Src MAC: the MAC of VTEP’s physical network interface that sending packets
[P8462|Item List] Dst MAC: MAC of the next hop to destination VTEP IP.
[P8463|Item List] VLAN: if the under layer physical network uses VLAN interface, then it can take the corresponding VLAN TAG optionally.
[P8464|Heading 6] Forwarding Theory - Broadcast in Layer 2
[P8465|Normal] 
[P8466|Figure Description] The process of broadcast packets forwarding
[P8467|Body Text] As shown in the figure above, HOST A and HOST B are in the same network segment but distributes in different VTEP, the detail networking process for HOST A and HOST B is the following:
[P8468|Item List] HOST A and HOST B are in the same network segment, HOST A sends ARP to request the MAC address of HOST B
[P8469|Item List] When ARP requested packet reaches to VTEP-1, switch finds that it is a broadcast packet and need to flood in VLAN, and one copy of this packet is sent to VXLAN tunnel (broadcast copies on the head VTEP, if there are several tunnels, it will send one packet to each tunnel). VLAN maps to VNI with VXLAN capsulate, it will add the external UDP IP encapsulation, according the external IP searching routing table to make sure the next hop of this packet. Switch will learn address MAC-A to interface eth-0-1 in corresponding VLAN at the same time
[P8470|Item List] Packet is forwarding depends on the external IP; it will reach to VTEP-2 at last.
[P8471|Item List] After VTEP-2 receives this packet, it will find that the outer D-mac is the local address, meanwhile, it will check whether local has configured corresponding tunnel by packet’s Outer S-IP, Outer D-IP and VNI. If it has the tunnel, then it will take decapsulated operation, cut the outer header and map VNI into corresponding VLAN; it will broadcast in VLAN when it finds it is broadcast packet. At the same time, it will learn Mac-A to relevant tunnel interface in VLAN.
[P8472|Heading 6] Forwarding Theory - Unicast in Layer 2
[P8473|Normal] 
[P8474|Figure Description] The process of unicast packets forwarding
[P8475|Body Text] As shown in the figure above, HOST B replies the ARP request sent from HOST A; this packet is unicast packet, the following example shows the process of unicast packet forwarding:
[P8476|Item List] HOST B sends ARP reply; it will reach to switch VTEP-2 by eth-0-1.
[P8477|Item List] On VTEP-2, it will find that the outbound interface of MAC-B is VXLAN tunnel in this VLAN, and remote terminal VTEP is 10.1.1.1 by searching mac address table using Dst-mac; then map the VLAN where the original packet is in to VNI and add the header of VXLAN, and add outer MAC/IP header, Outer S-IP as local VTEP IP, Outer D-IP ad remote terminal VTEP IP, Outer S-mac as local outbound interface’s mac, Outer D-mac as the next hop’s interface mac for Outer D-IP.
[P8478|Item List] Packet is forwarding according to outer IP in the network, it will reach to VTEP-1 finally.
[P8479|Item List] After VTEP-1 receives packet and finds that the Outer D-mac is the local address, it will examine whether it configures the relevant tunnel by packet’s Outer S-IP, Outer D-IP and VNI. If it has configured, then it will take decapsulation action to cut the outer header and map VNI to corresponding VLAN, and search the mac address table through original packet’s Dst-mac (MAC-A); then it will find that the outbound interface of Mac-A is eth-0-1, then it will send the packet after decapsulating through eth-0-1. Meanwhile, it learns Mac-B to relevant tunnel interface in VLAN.
[P8480|Normal] By default, VTEP has tunnels that connect with each other; if it finds that the exit of Dst-mac is tunnel after decapsulating, then the packet will be discard.
[P8481|Heading 6] Forwarding Theory - Concentrated VXLAN network gateway
[P8482|Normal] 
[P8483|Figure Description] Diagram of concentrated gateway
[P8484|Body Text] As shown in the figure above, HOST A and B are in different network section, network between them need the help from network gateway. In this situation, it can configure the network gateway onto VTEP-3 intensively, VTEP-1 and VTEP-2 will create VXLAN tunnels to VTEP-3 separately, and then the administrators can make managements intensively.
[P8485|Item List] HOST A sends arp-request to request the mac address of gateway, VTEP-1 will do vxlan encapsulation to this arp-requestand then forward to VTEP-3 as unknown unicast traffic.
[P8486|Item List] VTEP-3 will determine whether itself has the gateway address that the packet requested after it receives the arp-request,if it does then it replies arp-reply with vxlan encapsulation to HOST A and learn arp entry of HOST A, its outbound interface is vxlan tunnel.
[P8487|Item List] VTEP-1 will cut the header of vxlan after it receives this arp-reply; it will forward the original arp-reply to HOST A and learn the mac address of gateway and its outbound interface is vxlan tunnel.
[P8488|Item List] When HOST A receives the arp-reply, it will learn the mac address of gateway and starts sending data packet. The format of data packet is shown in Figure 2-4.
[P8489|Item List] Gateway will determine if it needs to do routing forward or not after it receives this packet; however, there is no HOST B’s arp table items at this time. Therefore, it will send arp-request to request the arp of HOST B, this arp-request will add the vxlan header to VTEP-2.
[P8490|Item List] After VTEP-2 receiving the arp-request, it decapsultes and forwards to HOST B and learns the gateway’s mac address, its outbound interface is vxlan tunnel.
[P8491|Item List] HOST B replys arp-reply, its destination mac is the mac of gateway; it will search and forward on VTEP-2, and finds out the outbound interface is vxlan tunnel, hence VTEP-2 will do vxlan encapsulation of this packet and send it to gateway.
[P8492|Item List] After gateway receives this packet, it learns the arp of HOST B, and then forwards the data packet to HOST B through vxlan tunnel.
[P8493|Heading 6] Forwarding Theory - Distributed VXLAN network gateway
[P8494|Normal] 
[P8495|Figure Description] Diagram of distributed gateway
[P8496|Body Text] Rather than the routing function of concentrated gateway is done by a certain device, distributed gateway can spread the routing function into each VTEP it connects to, which will reduce the pressure of concentrated network gateway.
[P8497|Body Text] As shown in the figure above, network knows the IP-B is the host connects to VTEP-2, and the VXLAN ID is VXLAN-2. According to the information above, we can configure routing table on inbound VTEP (which is VTEP-1 in Figure 5), directly encapsulate packets and sent to IP-B , to reduce the pressure of gateway and reduce the delay time of forwarding at the same time. The detailed forwarding process is:
[P8498|Item List] HOST A sends packet Dst-ip as IP-B, since IP-B and this ip (IP-A) are not in the same network sections, hence this Dst-mac is gateway’s mac (Mac-C)
[P8499|Item List] When the packet gets to VTEP-1, VTEP-1 finds that the Dst-mac is the gateway mac in the network of VLAN, and then it will search whether it has the routing information of IP-B in routing table. If it exsits: then forwarding by the routing table, this route entry includes the VTEP and VXLAN ID information where IP-B is and the corresponding mac (Mac-B) information of IP-B. It will change the original packet’s Dst-mac to Mac-B on VTEP-1 and add the relevant encapsulation depends on outer packet information and then precede forwarding; if it does not exsit: then discard this packet
[P8500|Item List] Packet will forward according to outer packet in the network.
[P8501|Item List] Packet decapsulates when it reaches to VETP-2, the process of decapsulation is the same as Layer 2 forwarding.
[P8502|Normal] Distributed gateway needs the help from BGP EVPN to synchronize the arp table items on distributed gateway, or static configures DVR routing.
[P8503|Heading 5] Surrounding Features
[P8504|Heading 6] keep-vlan-tag
[P8505|Normal] By default, it will cut the VLAN tag which the original packet carries when encapsulation and map to outer VXLAN-VNI, and then encapsulated inner packet will not have VLAN tag anymore. If the packet enters the VXLAN network with multiple VLAN tags, it needs to keep the VLAN tag for original packet, the keep-vlan-tag properties should be enabled. For configuration in details, please refer to command line reference guide.
[P8506|Heading 6] tunnel-aware
[P8507|Normal] Packets that are encapsulated by VXLAN, traditional network devices can only recognize the outer header information of packet s and it will forward by outer header information. If congestions or other situations happen in the network, since it cannot recognize the inner information of packet s, it will not locate which virtual machine or server generates the congestion accurately. After enabling tunnel-aware function, it will allow switches to analyze the inner packet information of original packet, and then use this information on ACL, Flow tracing and so on, which will analyze network traffic accurately.
[P8508|Heading 6] Distributed-Gatway
[P8509|Normal] In distributed network gateway network, users can configure the gateway of server or virtual machine on to the VTEP which is directly connected. Networking between each virtual machine in different network sections will not use concentrated gateway anymore in the same VTEP. For example, cooperation with DVR routing will not deploy concentrated gateway, the detailed configuration method can be referred to the cases in chapter “Configuration Examples” of this document.
[P8510|Heading 6] split-horizon
[P8511|Normal] By default, we suggest that configure vxlan tunnels between vtep’s full mesh, the traffic from one tunnel cannot enter into another tunnel; if it has requirements of forwarding traffic with each other between tunnels, then disable the split-horizon on tunnels.
[P8512|Heading 6] Source address of tunnel
[P8513|Normal] By specifying sec-ip address when create tunnels, it can use different source IP address for different tunnels, a switch can accept up to four different source addresses.
[P8514|Heading 6] DSCP strategy
[P8515|Normal] When encapsulate, users can configure generate strategy of encapsulating packets’ DSCP, includes following options：fixed value, copy from original packet, map by priority of packet. The default option is copy from original packet.
[P8516|Normal] 
[P8517|Heading 3] Configuration
[P8518|Heading 4] Vxlan Configuration
[P8519|Normal] 
[P8520|Figure Description] Vxlan
[P8521|Body Text] In the following example, switch1 and swith2 are connected via layer 3 route. The traffic of vlan 20 are encapsulated in vni 20000, in order to pass through the layer 3 networks.
[P8522|Body Text] The following configuration should be operated on all switches if the switch ID is not specified.
[P8523|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P8524|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P8525|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan, enable overlay for each vlan
[P8526|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 20
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 20 overlay enable
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P8527|Heading 5] step 3 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface
[P8528|Normal] Interface configuration for Switch1:
[P8529|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 20
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 9.9.9.1/24
Switch(config-if)# overlay uplink enable
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface loopback0
Switch(config-if)# ip address 1.0.1.1/32
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P8530|Normal] Interface configuration for Switch2:
[P8531|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 20
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 9.9.9.2/24
Switch(config-if)# overlay uplink enable
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface loopback0
Switch(config-if)# ip address 1.0.1.2/32
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P8532|Heading 5] Step 4 Create a static route
[P8533|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8534|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ip route 1.0.1.2/32 9.9.9.2
[P8535|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8536|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# ip route 1.0.1.1/32 9.9.9.1
[P8537|Heading 5] Step 5 Set attributes for overlay
[P8538|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8539|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# overlay
Switch(config-overlay)# source 1.0.1.1
Switch(config-overlay)# remote-vtep 1 ip-address 1.0.1.2 type vxlan
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 vni 20000
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 remote-vtep 1
Switch(config-overlay)# exit
[P8540|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8541|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# overlay
Switch(config-overlay)# source 1.0.1.2
Switch(config-overlay)# remote-vtep 1 ip-address 1.0.1.1 type vxlan
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 vni 20000
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 remote-vtep 1
Switch(config-overlay)# exit
[P8542|Heading 5] step 6 Exit the configure mode
[P8543|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P8544|Heading 5] step 7 Validation

[P8549|Heading 4] Configuring VXLAN Routing
[P8550|Normal] 
[P8551|Figure Description] Vxlan
[P8552|Body Text] In the following example, VM-1 & VM-3 are encapsulated in same vni to make up the distributed route via vxlan; VM-2 & VM-4 are encapsulated in another vni to make up the distributed route via vxlan.
[P8553|Body Text] The following configuration should be operated on all switches if the switch ID is not specified.

Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 30 overlay enable
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P8558|Heading 5] step 3 Create a vrf instance

Switch(config-vrf)# exit
[P8560|Heading 5] step 4 Create the layer 3 interface and set the ip address

Switch(config-if)# ip address 3.3.3.111/24

Switch(config-if)# exit
[P8565|Heading 5] step 5 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface

[P8567|Normal] Configuring Switch1:

[P8569|Normal] Configuring Switch2:

Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 9.9.9.2/24
Switch(config-if)# overlay uplink enable
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config-if)# ip address 1.0.1.2/32
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P8571|Heading 5] Step 6 Set attributes for overlay
[P8572|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8573|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# overlay
Switch(config-overlay)# source 1.0.1.1
Switch(config-overlay)# remote-vtep 1 ip-address 1.0.1.2 type vxlan
Switch(config-overlay)# remote-vtep 1 virtual-mac 22.22.22
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 vni 20000
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 30 vni 30000
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 remote-vtep 1
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 30 remote-vtep 1
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 gateway-mac a.a.a
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 30 gateway-mac b.b.b
Switch(config-overlay)# exit
[P8574|Normal] Configuring Switch2:

Switch(config-overlay)# source 1.0.1.2
Switch(config-overlay)# remote-vtep 1 ip-address 1.0.1.1 type vxlan
Switch(config-overlay)# remote-vtep 1 virtual-mac 11.11.11
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 vni 20000
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 30 vni 30000
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 remote-vtep 1
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 30 remote-vtep 1
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 gateway-mac a.a.a
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 30 gateway-mac b.b.b
Switch(config-overlay)# exit
[P8576|Heading 5] step 7 Create a static routes and vxlan routes
[P8577|Normal] Configuring Switch1:

[P8588|Heading 4] Configuring VXLAN Distributed Routing by EBGP EVPN
[P8589|Normal] 
[P8590|Figure Description] EBGP_EVPN
[P8591|Body Text] In the following example, VM-1 & VM-2 are encapsulated in same vni to make up the distributed route via vxlan by EBGP EVPN for sending vxlan tunnel and host information;
[P8592|Body Text] The following configuration should be operated on all switches if the switch ID is not specified.
[P8593|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P8594|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P8595|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan, enable overlay for each vlan
[P8596|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 10, 20
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 10 overlay enable
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P8597|Normal] option: enable arp broadcast suppress for vlan
[P8598|Terminal Display] Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 10 arp-broadcast-suppress enable
[P8599|Heading 5] step 3 Create vlan mapping vni for vxlan
[P8600|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# overlay
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 10 vni 10000
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P8601|Normal] option: Disable inner fdb learning for overlay
[P8602|Terminal Display] Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 10 mac-address-tunnel learning-disable
[P8603|Heading 5] step 4 Create evpn instance
[P8604|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# evpn
Switch(config-evpn)# vni 10000
Switch(config-evi)# rd auto
Switch(config-evi)# route-target both 1:10000
Switch(config-evi)# exit
[P8605|Heading 5] step 5 Create a vrf instance, and enable EVPN
[P8606|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8607|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# ip vrf tenant
Switch1(config-vrf)# rd 1:20000
Switch1(config-vrf)# route-target both 1:10000 evpn
Switch1(config-vrf)# vxlan vni 20000
Switch1(config-vrf)# exit
[P8608|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8609|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# ip vrf tenant
Switch2(config-vrf)# rd 2:20000
Switch2(config-vrf)# route-target both 1:10000 evpn
Switch2(config-vrf)# vxlan vni 20000
Switch2(config-vrf)# exit
[P8610|Heading 5] step 6 Create the layer 3 interface ， set the ip address and enable distributed gateway
[P8611|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8612|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# interface  vlan 10
Switch1(config-if)# ip vrf forwarding tenant
Switch1(config-if)# overlay distributed-gateway enable
Switch1(config-if)# overlay host-collect enable
Switch1(config-if)# ip address 10.1.1.1/24
Switch1(config-if)# exit
Switch1(config)# interface  vlan 20
Switch1(config-if)# ip address 20.1.1.1/24
Switch1(config-if)# exit
[P8613|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8614|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# interface  vlan 10
Switch2(config-if)# ip vrf forwarding tenant
Switch2(config-if)# overlay distributed-gateway enable
Switch2(config-if)# overlay host-collect enable
Switch2(config-if)# ip address 10.1.1.2/24
Switch2(config-if)# exit
Switch2(config)# interface  vlan 20
Switch2(config-if)# ip address 20.1.1.2/24
Switch2(config-if)# exit
[P8615|Heading 5] step 7 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface
[P8616|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add  20
Switch(config-if)# vxlan uplink enable
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P8617|Heading 5] Step 8 Create NVE
[P8618|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8619|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# interface loopback 1
Switch1(config-if)# ip address 1.1.1.1/32
Switch1(config-if)# exit
Switch1(config)# interface nve 1
Switch1(config-if)# source loopback 1
Switch1(config-if)# member vni 10000

Switch1(config-if)# exit
[P8620|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8621|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# interface loopback 1
Switch2(config-if)# ip address 2.2.2.2/32

Switch2(config-if)# member vni 10000
Switch2(config-if)# member vni 20000 associate-vrf
Switch2(config-if)# exit
[P8622|Normal] option: configure the attribute of EVPN tunnel

Switch(config-if)# split-horizon disable
Switch(config-if)# encapsulation-dscp-strategy custom-assign 63

[P8629|Heading 5] step 10 Create a static routes

[P8641|Heading 4] Configuring VXLAN Distributed Routing by IBGP EVPN
[P8642|Normal] 
[P8643|Figure Description] IBGP_EVPN
[P8644|Body Text] In the following example, VM-1 & VM-2 are encapsulated in same vni to make up the distributed route via vxlan by IBGP EVPN for sending vxlan tunnel and host information;EVPN route is exchanged by bgp route reflector.
[P8645|Body Text] The following configuration should be operated on all switches if the switch ID is not specified.
[P8646|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P8647|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P8648|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan, enable overlay for each vlan
[P8649|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8650|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# vlan database
Switch1(config-vlan)# vlan 10, 20
Switch1(config-vlan)# vlan 10 overlay enable
Switch1(config-vlan)# exit
[P8651|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8652|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# vlan database
Switch2(config-vlan)# vlan 20, 30
Switch2(config-vlan)# exit
[P8653|Normal] Configuring Switch3:
[P8654|Terminal Display] Switch3(config)# vlan database
Switch3(config-vlan)# vlan 10, 30
Switch3(config-vlan)# vlan 10 overlay enable
Switch3(config-vlan)# exit
[P8655|Normal] option: enable arp broadcast suppress for vlan
[P8656|Terminal Display] Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 10 arp-broadcast-suppress enable
[P8657|Heading 5] step 3 Create vlan mapping vni for vxlan
[P8658|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8659|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# overlay
Switch1(config-overlay)# vlan 10 vni 10000
Switch1(config-vlan)# exit
[P8660|Normal] option: Disable inner fdb learning for overlay
[P8661|Terminal Display] Switch1(config-overlay)# vlan 10 mac-address-tunnel learning-disable
[P8662|Normal] Configuring Switch3:
[P8663|Terminal Display] Switch3(config)# overlay
Switch3(config-overlay)# vlan 10 vni 10000
Switch3(config-vlan)# exit
[P8664|Normal] option: Disable inner fdb learning for overlay
[P8665|Terminal Display] Switch3(config-overlay)# vlan 10 mac-address-tunnel learning-disable
[P8666|Heading 5] step 4 Create evpn instance
[P8667|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8668|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# evpn
Switch1(config-evpn)# vni 10000
Switch1(config-evi)# rd 2:2
Switch1(config-evi)# route-target both 20:20
Switch1(config-evi)# exit
[P8669|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8670|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# evpn
[P8671|Normal] Configuring Switch3:
[P8672|Terminal Display] Switch3(config)# evpn
Switch3(config-evpn)# vni 10000
Switch3(config-evi)# rd 4:4
Switch3(config-evi)# route-target both 20:20
Switch3(config-evi)# exit
[P8673|Heading 5] step 5 Create a vrf instance, and enable EVPN
[P8674|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8675|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# ip vrf tenant
Switch1(config-vrf)# rd 22:22
Switch1(config-vrf)# route-target both 20:20 evpn
Switch1(config-vrf)# vxlan vni 20000
Switch1(config-vrf)# exit
[P8676|Normal] 在switch3配置：
[P8677|Body Text] Configuring Switch3:
[P8678|Terminal Display] Switch3(config)# ip vrf tenant
Switch3(config-vrf)# rd 44:44
Switch3(config-vrf)# route-target both 20:20 evpn
Switch3(config-vrf)# vxlan vni 20000
Switch3(config-vrf)# exit
[P8679|Heading 5] step 6 Create the layer 3 interface ， set the ip address and enable distributed gateway
[P8680|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8681|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# interface  vlan 10
Switch1(config-if)# ip vrf forwarding tenant
Switch1(config-if)# overlay distributed-gateway enable
Switch1(config-if)# overlay host-collect enable
Switch1(config-if)# ip address 10.1.1.2/24
Switch1(config-if)# exit
Switch1(config)# interface  vlan 20
Switch1(config-if)# ip address 20.1.1.1/24
Switch1(config-if)# exit
[P8682|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8683|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# interface  vlan 20
Switch2(config-if)# ip address 20.1.1.2/24
Switch2(config-if)# exit
Switch2(config)# interface  vlan 30
Switch2(config-if)# ip address 30.1.1.1/24
Switch2(config-if)# exit
[P8684|Normal] Configuring Switch3:
[P8685|Terminal Display] Switch3(config)# interface  vlan 10
Switch3(config-if)# ip vrf forwarding tenant
Switch3(config-if)# overlay distributed-gateway enable
Switch3(config-if)# overlay host-collect enable
Switch3(config-if)# ip address 10.1.1.3/24
Switch3(config-if)# exit 
Switch3(config)# interface  vlan 30
Switch3(config-if)# ip address 30.1.1.2/24
Switch3(config-if)# exit
[P8686|Heading 5] step 7 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface
[P8687|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8688|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# interface eth-0-10
Switch1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
Switch1(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch1(config-if)# exit
Switch1(config)# interface eth-0-20
Switch1(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add  20
Switch1(config-if)# vxlan uplink enable
Switch1(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch1(config-if)# exit
[P8689|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8690|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# interface eth-0-20
Switch2(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch2(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add  20
Switch2(config-if)# vxlan uplink enable
Switch2(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch2(config-if)# exit
Switch2(config)# interface eth-0-30
Switch2(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch2(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add  30
Switch2(config-if)# vxlan uplink enable
Switch2(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch2(config-if)# exit
[P8691|Normal] Configuring Switch3:
[P8692|Terminal Display] Switch3(config)# interface eth-0-10
Switch3(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
Switch3(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch3(config-if)# exit
Switch3(config)# interface eth-0-30
Switch3(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch3(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add  30
Switch3(config-if)# vxlan uplink enable
Switch3(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch3(config-if)# exit
[P8693|Heading 5] Step 8 Create NVE
[P8694|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8695|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# interface loopback 2
Switch1(config-if)# ip address 2.2.2.2/32
Switch1(config-if)# exit
Switch1(config)# interface nve 1
Switch1(config-if)# source 2.2.2.2
Switch1(config-if)# member vni 10000
Switch1(config-if)# member vni 20000 associate-vrf
Switch1(config-if)# exit
[P8696|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8697|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# interface loopback 3
Switch2(config-if)# ip address 3.3.3.3/32
Switch2(config-if)# exit
[P8698|Normal] Configuring Switch3:
[P8699|Terminal Display] Switch3(config)# interface loopback 4
Switch3(config-if)# ip address 4.4.4.4/32
Switch3(config-if)# exit
Switch3(config)# interface nve 1
Switch3(config-if)# source 4.4.4.4
Switch3(config-if)# member vni 10000
Switch3(config-if)# member vni 20000 associate-vrf
Switch3(config-if)# exit
[P8700|Normal] option: configure the attribute of EVPN tunnel
[P8701|Terminal Display] Switch(config-if)# keep-vlan-tag enable
Switch(config-if)# split-horizon disable
Switch(config-if)# encapsulation-dscp-strategy custom-assign 63
Switch(config-if)# virtual-mac a.a.a
[P8702|Heading 5] Step 9 Create BGP EVPN
[P8703|Normal] Configuring Switch1:
[P8704|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# router bgp 100
Switch1(config-router)# neighbor 3.3.3.3 remote-as 100
Switch1(config-router)# neighbor 3.3.3.3 update-source loopback2
Switch1(config-router)# neighbor 20.1.1.2 remote-as 100
Switch1(config-router)# address-family ipv4
Switch1(config-router-af)# network 2.2.2.2 mask 255.255.255.255
Switch1(config-router-af)# neighbor 20.1.1.2 weight 32768
Switch1(config-router-af)# exit
Switch1(config-router)# address-family l2vpn evpn
Switch1(config-router-af)# neighbor 3.3.3.3 activate
Switch1(config-router-af)# neighbor 3.3.3.3 send-community extended
Switch1(config-router-af)# exit
Switch1(config-router)# exit
[P8705|Normal] Configuring Switch2:
[P8706|Terminal Display] Switch2(config)# router bgp 100
Switch2(config-router)# neighbor 2.2.2.2 remote-as 100
Switch2(config-router)# neighbor 2.2.2.2 update-source loopback3
Switch2(config-router)# neighbor 4.4.4.4 remote-as 100
Switch2(config-router)# neighbor 4.4.4.4 update-source loopback3
Switch2(config-router)# neighbor 20.1.1.1 remote-as 100
Switch2(config-router)# neighbor 30.1.1.2 remote-as 100
Switch2(config-router)# address-family ipv4
Switch2(config-router-af)# network 3.3.3.3 mask 255.255.255.255
Switch2(config-router-af)# network 20.1.1.0 mask 255.255.255.0
Switch2(config-router-af)# network 30.1.1.0 mask 255.255.255.0
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 20.1.1.1 weight 32768
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 20.1.1.1 route-reflector-client
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 30.1.1.2 weight 32768
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 30.1.1.2 route-reflector-client
Switch2(config-router-af)# exit
Switch2(config-router)# address-family l2vpn evpn
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 2.2.2.2 activate
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 2.2.2.2 route-reflector-client
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 2.2.2.2 send-community extended
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 4.4.4.4 activate
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 4.4.4.4 route-reflector-client
Switch2(config-router-af)# neighbor 4.4.4.4 send-community extended
Switch2(config-router-af)# exit
Switch2(config-router)# exit
[P8707|Normal] 
[P8708|Normal] Configuring Switch3:
[P8709|Terminal Display] Switch3(config)# router bgp 100
Switch3(config-router)# neighbor 3.3.3.3 remote-as 100
Switch3(config-router)# neighbor 3.3.3.3 update-source loopback4
Switch3(config-router)# neighbor 30.1.1.1 remote-as 100
Switch3(config-router)# address-family ipv4
Switch3(config-router-af)# network 4.4.4.4 mask 255.255.255.255
Switch3(config-router-af)# neighbor 30.1.1.1 weight 32768
Switch3(config-router-af)# exit
Switch3(config-router)# address-family l2vpn evpn
Switch3(config-router-af)# neighbor 3.3.3.3 activate
Switch3(config-router-af)# neighbor 3.3.3.3 send-community extended
Switch3(config-router-af)# exit
Switch3(config-router)# exit
[P8710|Heading 5] step 10 Exit the configure mode
[P8711|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end

[P8719|Heading 4] 	Users In the same network segment communicate through VXLAN Network
[P8720|Heading 5] Topology
[P8721|Normal] 
[P8722|Figure Description] VXLAN network communication
[P8723|Heading 5] Requirement
[P8724|Normal] Host 1 and Host 2 are in the same segment, they need to realize interflow by VXLAN tunnels.
[P8725|Heading 5] Configuration Steps
[P8726|Step] Configure routing on SWITCH A/SWITCH B/SWITCH C, make sure that these three switches can interflow with each other in Layer 3 network
[P8727|Body Text] configure SWITCH A
[P8728|Terminal Display] SWITCH_A# configure terminal 
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
SWITCH_A(config)# interface loopback 0
SWITCH_A(config-if)# ip address 10.1.1.1/32
SWITCH_A(config-if)# exit
SWITCH_A(config)# interface eth-0-9
SWITCH_A(config-if)# no switchport 
SWITCH_A(config-if)# ip address 192.168.1.1/24
SWITCH_A(config-if)# vxlan uplink enable
SWITCH_A(config-if)# no shutdown 
SWITCH_A(config-if)# exit
SWITCH_A(config)# ip route 10.3.3.3/32 192.168.1.2
SWITCH_A(config)# end

SWITCH_B(config-if)# no shutdown 
SWITCH_B(config-if)# exit

SWITCH_B(config-if)# no switchport

SWITCH_B(config-if)# exit

SWITCH_B(config)# ip route 10.3.3.3/32 192.168.2.2
SWITCH_B(config)# end

[P8738|Step] Configure VXLAN tunnels on SWITCH A/SWITCH C
[P8739|Body Text] configure SWITCH A

[P8741|Normal] configure SWITCH C

Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.

[P8748|Heading 4] Concentrated VXLAN Gateway
[P8749|Heading 5] Topology
[P8750|Normal] 
[P8751|Figure Description] Concentrated VXLAN gateway networking diagram
[P8752|Heading 5] Requirement
[P8753|Normal] As shown in the figure, HOST1/2/3 are all belong to tenement test, it has the same segments and different segments, and they all need interflow with each other. Between Switch A Switch B and Switch C is Layer 3 network, so it needs to create tunnels by configuring VXLAN between HOST, and realizes networking between HOST by concentrated network gateway.
[P8754|Body Text] It can select SWITCH B as the concentrated network gateway.

[P8789|Heading 3] Deployment Suggestion
[P8790|Heading 4] Active-Active Connect to VXLAN Network and Distributed Gateway
[P8791|Heading 5] Topology
[P8792|Normal] 
[P8793|Figure Description] Active-active connects to VXLAN and distributed gateway
[P8794|Heading 5] Requirement
[P8795|Normal] From the diagram, Switch A/B/C are TOR switches, between them is Layer 3 network, the downlink HOST are tenement test, it requires to isolate with other tenements. To make sure the reliabilities, part of the servers need active-active connection, so it needs to configure MLAG and configure virtual ip as server’s gateway on SWITCH A/B. At the same time, making sure the gateway address is not changing after virtual machine migration, and then deploy distributed gateway on SWITCH A/B/C.

[P8855|Heading 2] Configuring NVGRE
[P8856|Heading 3] Overview
[P8857|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P8858|Normal] Network Virtualization using Generic Routing Encapsulation (NVGRE) is an encapsulation technique intended to allow virtual network overlays across the physical network. NVGRE uses Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) as the encapsulation method. It uses the lower 24 bits of the GRE header to represent the Tenant Network Identifier (TNI.) Like VXLAN this 24 bit space allows for 16 million virtual networks.
[P8859|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P8860|Normal] N/A
[P8861|Heading 3] Configuration
[P8862|Heading 4] NVGRE Configuration
[P8863|Normal] 
[P8864|Figure Description] NVGRE
[P8865|Body Text] In the following example, switch1 and swith2 are connected via layer 3 route. The traffic of vlan 20 are encapsulated in vni 20000, in order to pass through the layer 3 networks.
[P8866|Body Text] The following configuration should be operated on all switches if the switch ID is not specified.
[P8867|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P8868|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P8869|Heading 5] step 2 Enter the vlan configure mode and create vlan, enable overlay for each vlan

Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 20
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 20 overlay enable
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
[P8871|Heading 5] step 3 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface
[P8872|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 20

Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2

Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config-if)# no switchport

Switch(config-if)# overlay uplink enable
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 20 remote-vtep 1
Switch(config-overlay)# vlan 30 remote-vtep 1

[P8933|Heading 2] Configuring GENEVE
[P8934|Heading 3] Overview
[P8935|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P8936|Normal] Generic Network Virtualization Encapsulation (GENEVE) is a networking technology that encapsulates MAC-based Layer 2 Ethernet frames within Layer 3 UDP packets to aggregate and tunnel multiple layer 2 networks across a Layer 3 infrastructure. GENEVE scales up to 16 million logical networks and supports layer 2 adjacency across IP networks. Multicast transmission architecture is used for broadcast/multicast/unknown packets.

[P8938|Normal] N/A

[P9011|Heading 2] Configuring Overlay
[P9012|Heading 3] Overview
[P9013|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P9014|Normal] Overlay function supports multiple source ip address of vtep, it can set different source ip for different networks and improve the reliability of overlay.
[P9015|Body Text] Overlay function also supports tunnel without horizon split, it means that when uplink port receiving tunnel packets and decapsulate them , and then send them into another tunnel for encapsulation.

[P9017|Normal] N/A

[P9095|Heading 1] Intelligent Lossless Network Configuration Guide
[P9096|Heading 2] Configuring Prioprity-based Flow Control
[P9097|Heading 3] Overview
[P9098|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P9099|Normal] In a network path that normally consists of multiple hops between source and destination, lack of feedback between transmitters and receivers at each hop is one of the main causes of unreliability. Transmitters can send packets faster than receivers accept packets, and as the receivers run out of available buffer space to absorb incoming flows, they are forced to silently drop all traffic that exceeds their capacity. These semantics work fine at Layer 2, so long as upper-layer protocols handle drop-detection and retransmission logic.
[P9100|Body Text] For applications that cannot build reliability on upper layers, the addition of flow control functions at Layer 2 can offer a solution. Flow control enables feedback from a receiver to its sender to communicate buffer availability. Its first implementation in IEEE 802.3 Ethernet uses the IEEE 802.3x PAUSE control frames. IEEE 802.3x PAUSE is defined in Annex 31B of the IEEE 802.3 specification. Simply put, a receiver can generate a MAC control frame and send a PAUSE request to a sender when it predicts the potential for buffer overflow. Upon receiving a PAUSE frame, the sender responds by stopping transmission of any new packets until the receiver is ready to accept them again.
[P9101|Body Text] IEEE 802.3x PAUSE works as designed, but it suffers a basic disadvantage that limits its field of applicability: after a link is paused, a sender cannot generate any more packets. As obvious as that seems, the consequence is that the application of IEEE 802.3x PAUSE makes an Ethernet segment unsuitable for carrying multiple traffic flows that might require different quality of service (QoS). Thus, enabling IEEE 802.3x PAUSE for one application can affect the performance of other network applications. IEEE 802.1Qbb PFC extends the basic IEEE 802.3x PAUSE semantics to multiple CoSs, enabling applications that require flow control to coexist on the same wire with applications that perform better without it. PFC uses the IEEE 802.1p CoS values in the IEEE 802.1Q VLAN tag to differentiate up to eight CoSs that can be subject to flow control independently.
[P9102|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P9103|Normal] N/A
[P9104|Heading 3] Configuration
[P9105|Normal] 
[P9106|Figure Description] Priority-based Flow Control
[P9107|Body Text] In the following example, interface eth-0-1 of switch1 and switch2 are connected, interface eth-0-2 of switch1 and switch2 are connected, all interface enable PFC for priority 2/3/4.
[P9108|Body Text] The following configuration are same for switch1 and 2.
[P9109|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P9110|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P9111|Heading 5] step 2 Enable lldp globally
[P9112|Terminal Display] Switch1(config)# lldp enable
[P9113|Heading 5] step 3 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface
[P9114|Terminal Display] Switch(config-if)#lldp enable txrx
Switch(config-if)# lldp tlv 8021-org-specific dcbx
Switch(config-if)# priority-flow-control mode  on
Switch(config-if)# priority-flow-control enable priority 2 3 4
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)#lldp enable txrx
Switch(config-if)# lldp tlv 8021-org-specific dcbx
Switch(config-if)# priority-flow-control mode  auto
Switch(config-if)# priority-flow-control enable priority 2 3 4 
Switch (config-if)# exit
[P9115|Heading 5] step 4 Exit the configure mode
[P9116|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end

[P9122|Heading 2] PFC deadlock detection configuration
[P9123|Heading 5] Step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P9124|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P9125|Heading 5] step 2 Configuring priority-flow-control deadlock precision (Optional)
[P9126|Body Text] The default precision is 10 milliseconds.
[P9127|Terminal Display] Switch# priority-flow-control deadlock precision 20
[P9128|Heading 5] step 3 Enable PFC deadlock detection
[P9129|Body Text] User can enable PFC deadlock detection for 1 or 2 priority on one interface.
[P9130|Body Text] User can specify the detect time multiple (with valid range 1-30). The precision value configured before multiples by this detect time multiple is the time period to determine the deadlock. During this time period, if the PAUSE OFF packets are received continuously, system will judge this priority of interface in PFC deadlock status. If the time multiple is not specified, system use the default value 15.
[P9131|Body Text] User can specify the recover time in the range of 0-3000 milliseconds. After this recover time, the deadlock is resolved and system start to detect again. The default recover time is 150 milliseconds.
[P9132|Body Text] The following example enables PFC deadlock detection on priority 5/6 of the interface eth-0-1. The detect multiple is 20, so according to the precision 20 milliseconds, the deadlock period should be 400 milliseconds. If the interface eth-0-1 received PAUSE OFF for priority 5 or 6 in continuously in 400 milliseconds, it will in deadlock status. The deadlock status will recover in 300 milliseconds. (But it may enter deadlock status again after 400 milliseconds)
[P9133|Body Text] In The deadlock status, system does NOT deal with the PAUSE OFF messages.
[P9134|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# priority-flow-control deadlock priority 5 6 detect 20 recover 300
[P9135|Heading 5] step 4  Limit the PFC deadlock detection function(Optional)
[P9136|Body Text] User can enable the deadlock limit feature. It can enable for 1 or 2 priority on one interface.
[P9137|Body Text] User can specify the deadlock times and detect period. If the deadlock times achieve the threshold in the specified period, system will disable PFC for this priority of the interface, and wait for the administrator to deal with the network abnormal condition.
[P9138|Body Text] The default threshold is 10 times in 1 minute.
[P9139|Body Text] The following example enables PFC deadlock limit on priority 5/6 of interface eth-0-1, if deadlock 100 times in 5 minutes, system should disable PFC for this priority.
[P9140|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# priority-flow-control deadlock limit priority 5 6 frequency 100 period 5
[P9141|Normal] 
[P9142|Heading 2] Configuring EFD
[P9143|Heading 3] Overview
[P9144|Heading 4] Function Introduction
[P9145|Normal] Elephant Flow Detect (EFD). According to the academic institutions of the actual network of the study found that more than 80% of the bandwidth is occupied by elephant flow, the bandwidth and transmission cache of these flow is large, but not sensitive to delay, which is sensitive to delay The flow caused a great impact. If elephant flow is recognized and some forwarding policies are implemented (such as reducing the forwarding priority of elephant flow appropriately, let mice flow be forwarded first), it can improve the transmission efficiency of network.
[P9146|Body Text] EFD function can be used to detect some abnormal traffic in the network (such as large bandwidth flow). After detecting, you can encapsulate the characteristics in the protocol packets and sent it to the specified server for further analysis.
[P9147|Heading 4] Principle Description
[P9148|Normal] terminology：
[P9149|Item List] EFD：Elephant Flow Detect
[P9150|Heading 3] Configuration
[P9151|Normal] 
[P9152|Figure Description] EFD
[P9153|Body Text] In the following example, it specifies the characteristics field and threshold of the traffic. When the flow rate exceed the specified threshold, the characteristics of the packets will be encapsulated into the user-defined UDP packets and sent to the server.
[P9154|Heading 5] step 1 Enter the configure mode
[P9155|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P9156|Heading 5] step 1 Set the parameters for EFC
[P9157|Normal] Specify ipda to calculate packet’s hash value
[P9158|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# hash-value global
Switch(config-hash-value-global)# efd select ipda
[P9159|Normal] Configure the speed threshold of EFD. The flows which has the rate large than 1000Mbps will be marked as Elephant Flow. The default value is 50Mbps.
[P9160|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# efd detect speed 1000
[P9161|Normal] Enable EFD notify feature, and specify the ipda and UDP port of notification packet
[P9162|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# efd notify enable 10.0.0.2 20007
[P9163|Heading 5] step 3 Enter the interface configure mode and set the attributes of the interface
[P9164|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1/1
Switch(config-if)# efd enable
Switch(config-if)# exit

Switch(config)# int eth-0-1/2
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.0.0.1/24
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P9165|Heading 5] step 4 Create a static arp entry (Optional)
[P9166|Terminal Display]  Switch(config)# arp 10.0.0.2 0.1.2
[P9167|Heading 5] step 5 Exit the configure mode
[P9168|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# end
[P9169|Heading 5] step 6 Validation
[P9170|Terminal Display] Switch# show efd configuration 
Elephant flow detection configuration information:
--------------------------------------------------
Detect rate            : 1000 Mbps
Detect granularity     : 16B
Detect time interval   : 1000 ms
EFD aging time         : 120 ms ~ 150 ms
EFD detect packet type : All IP packets
EFD IPG                : disable
EFD redirect interface : N/A
EFD flow hash fields   : destination-ip
EFD enabled interface : 
------------------------- -------------------------
eth-0-1/1

[P9175|Normal] EFD packet head description. The red part above is part of EFD packet information, specific analysis is as follows:
[P9176|Item List] 0000: reserved, no specific meaning. Part of EFD packet head.
[P9177|Item List] 01:EFD packt version number, only support 0x01. Part of EFD packet head.
[P9178|Item List] 01:EFD flow opcode, 0x01: This flow is first recognized as elephant flow. 0x02: This flow has been recognized as elephant flow before. Part of EFD packet head.

[P9183|Heading 2] ConfiguringECN
[P9184|Heading 3] Overview
[P9185|Heading 4] Brief Introduction
[P9186|Heading 5] ECN (Configuring Explicit Congestion Notification)
[P9187|Normal] Congestion occurs when the bandwidth of the downstream link of the forwarding device is insufficient to carry the traffic of the upstream link.As the congestion continues, the queue cache of the forwarding device is gradually compressed until it is exhausted. In this case, packet loss occurs.To solve this problem, RFC3168 defines Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) to inform traffic senders to slow down the sending speed and bring the problem under control before packet loss.
[P9188|Normal] 
[P9189|Figure Description] ToS Field
[P9190|Body Text] Eight bits are allocated in the ToS field of the IP packet header.
[P9191|Body Text] Bits 0 to 2 represent the eight priorities of IP packets. Priorities 7 and 6 are generally used to carry protocol packets.
[P9192|Body Text] Bits 0-5 are the DSCP of IP packets and define more service types.
[P9193|Body Text] Bits 6-7 are ECN fields.The values and meanings of ECN are as follows:
[P9194|Item List] If the ECN field is 00, the message does not support ECN.
[P9195|Item List] If the ECN field is 01 or 10, the packet supports ECN.
[P9196|Item List] If the ECN field is 11, it indicates that congestion occurs on the path.
[P9197|Normal] Therefore, the ECN mechanism is as follows: When the intermediate switch is congested, the ECN flag is set to 11, and packets continue to be transmitted downstream.When a packet reaches the receiving end, the receiving end finds that the ECN field is 11 and considers that there is congestion in the path. Therefore, the receiving end sends CNP(Congestion Notification Packet) to the sending end to request the sending end to reduce the sending rate to prevent congestion
[P9198|Normal] 
[P9199|Figure Description] ECN mechanism
[P9200|Heading 3] Configuration Examples
[P9201|Heading 4] Configuration of ECN on priority queues
[P9202|Heading 5] Configuration Steps
[P9203|Normal] In the following example, ECN is configured on queue1,4,6 of Switch1. The threshould of queue4’s ecn is 2100 and 5000. Other ecn threshould is configured as default value.
[P9204|Step] Enter the configure mode
[P9205|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
[P9206|Step] Configure priority mapping
[P9207|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# class-map type qos pri-4
Switch(config-cmap-qos)# match dscp ef
Switch(config-cmap-qos)# exit
Switch(config)# class-map type qos pri-6
Switch(config-cmap-qos)# match dscp cs6
Switch(config-cmap-qos)# exit
Switch(config)# class-map type qos pri-1
Switch(config-cmap-qos)# match dscp cs1
Switch(config-cmap-qos)# exit
Switch(config)# policy-map type qos pri-pmap
Switch(config-pmap-qos)# class type qos pri-4
Switch(config-pmap-qos-c)# set traffic-class 4
Switch(config-pmap-qos-c)# exit
Switch(config-pmap-qos)# class type qos pri-6
Switch(config-pmap-qos-c)# set traffic-class 6
Switch(config-pmap-qos-c)# exit
Switch(config-pmap-qos)# class type qos pri-1
Switch(config-pmap-qos-c)# set traffic-class 1
Switch(config-pmap-qos-c)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# service-policy type qos input pri-pmap
Switch(config-if)# end
[P9208|Step] Configure queue scheduling and ECN threshould
[P9209|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# class-map type traffic-class traffic-pri-4
Switch(config-cmap-tc)# match traffic-class 4
Switch(config-cmap-tc)# class-map type traffic-class traffic-pri-6
Switch(config-cmap-tc)# match traffic-class 6
Switch(config-cmap-tc)# class-map type traffic-class traffic-pri-1
Switch(config-cmap-tc)# match traffic-class 1
Switch(config-cmap-tc)# exit
Switch(config)# policy-map type traffic-class traffic-pmap
Switch(config-pmap-tc)# class type traffic-class traffic-pri-4
Switch(config-pmap-tc-c)# random-detect maximum-threshold 5000 minimum-threshold 2100 ecn
Switch(config-pmap-tc-c)# class type traffic-class traffic-pri-6
Switch(config-pmap-tc-c)# random-detect maximum-threshold 8192 minimum-threshold 64 ecn
Switch(config-pmap-tc-c)# class type traffic-class traffic-pri-1
Switch(config-pmap-tc-c)# random-detect maximum-threshold 8192 minimum-threshold 64 ecn
Switch(config-pmap-tc)# class type traffic-class class-default
Switch(config-pmap-tc-c)# queue-limit dynamic 5
Switch(config-pmap-tc-c)# exit
Switch(config-pmap-tc)# exit
[P9210|Step] Apply this ecn policy on an interface
[P9211|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1 
Switch(config-if)# service-policy type traffic-class traffic-pmap
Switch(config-if)# exit
[P9212|Step] Exit the configure mode
[P9213|Normal] Switch(config)# end
